english: Now, therefore, we shall expound the putrakāmīya (relating to one who desires a son) Śārīra (relating to the body).

text_flags.why: possible: short i printed for long ī (putra-kāma + -īya)

hindi: अब इक्कीस वर्ष का पुरुष असमान गोत्र की, असमान वंश की, ऐसे कुल में उत्पन्न जिसमें रोग संचारी नहीं है, रूप, शील और लक्षणों से सम्पन्न, न्यून न होने वाली, जिसके दाँत, होंठ, कान, नख, केश और स्तन नष्ट न हुए हों, जिसकी प्रकृति कोमल और रोगरहित हो, जो न कपिला हो न पिंगला, जिसके अंग न हीन हों न अधिक, जो लगभग बारह वर्ष की हो, जो देवता, सर्प, नदी, चल वस्तु, वृक्ष, पक्षी, नक्षत्र तथा अन्य न देखने योग्य और भयानक वस्तुओं के नाम धारण न करती हो, निर्दोष और निन्दा से रहित कन्या को निन्दारहित विधि से ब्याहे।
english: Now, a man of twenty-one years should marry, by a blameless rule, a girl of unlike gotra and of unlike ancestry, born in a family in which disease is non-transmitting; endowed with beauty, conduct and marks; not deficient; whose teeth, lips, ears, nails, hair and breasts are undamaged; whose constitution (prakṛti) is gentle and free of disease; not tawny and not reddish-brown; with limbs neither deficient nor in excess; of about twelve years; not bearing names of immortals, serpents, rivers, moving things, trees, birds, stars, or of other things not to be looked at and frightening; faultless and blameless.

text_flags.why: print spacing: the final m of aniṃdyām stands at the start of the next printed token
stray m belongs to the preceding word aniṃdyām
possible: extra 'du' (or vidhinodvahet); sense 'by rule, should marry'
possible: masculine mṛdum beside feminine accusatives; ā in arogā- also doubtful

notes: Long single prose sentence; subject pumān, verb udvahet at the end. Parse points: (1) atulya = 'unlike' (the text does not say 'not of his own'); the sense is probably 'not of his own gotra and ancestry'. (2) asaṃcāri-roga-kula: literally 'disease non-transmitting, family'; the sense is probably a family without hereditary disease, not certain. (3) mṛdu-aroga-prakṛti: reading uncertain, see text_flags. (4) ahīna-adhika-aṅgī: literally 'not deficient, in excess, limbed'; the plainer sense is 'neither deficient nor excessive in limbs'. (5) deśīya = approximately. (6) the name-list: 'nakṣatrānyaprekṣyabhīṣaṇakanāmāni' could also be read nakṣatra-nāmāni, anya-aprekṣya-bhīṣaṇaka-nāmāni; the rendering 'of other things not to be looked at and frightening' is one reading. cala is rendered 'moving things'; its exact referent is not stated.

hindi: उसमें, जो सोलह वर्ष की है, पच्चीस वर्ष का पुरुष पुत्र के लिए प्रयत्न करे।
english: In her, of sixteen years, a man of twenty-five years should strive for the sake of a son.
notes: Ages are translated as printed (unit 5 says the girl is of about twelve years; this unit says sixteen). The two statements are not reconciled here. 'tasyām' refers back to the kanyā of unit 5.
lines_deva: तस्यां षोडशवर्षीयां पंचविंशतिवर्षः पुरुषः पुत्रार्थं प्रयतेत
lines_iast: tasyāṃ ṣoḍaśavarṣīyāṃ paṃcaviṃśativarṣaḥ puruṣaḥ putrārthaṃ prayateta

hindi: क्योंकि तब वे दोनों वीर्य यानी शक्ति को प्राप्त होकर शक्ति से युक्त सन्तान को उत्पन्न करते हैं।
english: For then those two, having attained potency (vīrya), beget offspring endowed with potency.
notes: 'vīrya' is rendered 'potency' (vigor), not semen; the text does not say 'semen' here. The printed token vīryānvitamapatyaṃ is vīrya-anvitam apatyam; split into two words below.
lines_deva: तदा हि तौ प्राप्तवीर्यौ वीर्यान्वितमपत्यं जनयतः
lines_iast: tadā hi tau prāptavīryau vīryānvitamapatyaṃ janayataḥ

hindi: पच्चीस वर्ष से कम आयु वाले पुरुष द्वारा सोलह वर्ष से कम आयु वाली में स्थापित गर्भ कोख में ही, अनुमानित पाठ पर, नाश को प्राप्त हो जाए, या अल्पायु तथा बल, आरोग्य और साधनों से हीन हो, या विकल इन्द्रियों वाला हो; और ऋतु में, पहली तीन रात्रियों में, तथा दूषित होने पर, अनुमानित पाठ पर, शुक्र और आर्तव का क्षय।
english: An embryo (garbha) placed by one of less than twenty-five years in one of less than sixteen years may reach destruction in the womb itself (kukṣisthaḥ, on a conjectural reading of the printed kukṣisya), or may be of short life-span, with little strength, health and means, or with defective sense organs; and in the ṛtu, in the first triad of nights, and likewise when it is vitiated, on a conjectural reading, injury of semen and menstrual blood (śukra and ārtava).

text_flags.why: possible: 'kukṣisya' is not a word; 'kukṣisthaḥ' (staying in the womb) fits sense and the following eva; th/y confusion
possible: ṃ for a; vikala-indriya 'with defective senses'
possible: final word is unclear; no sure restoration (śukra-ārtava with hati 'injury' is only a guess)

notes: Heavy sentence; the last token śukrārtavahati is unrestorable with confidence: kept unsplit and marked unclear; the translation of the end is on a conjectural reading ('injury of semen and menstrual blood'). 'ṛtau ādye ca rātritraye' is rendered literally ('in the ṛtu, and in the first triad of nights'); the intended sense (first three nights of the menstrual period) is not stated by the words. ṛtu = the woman's fertile or menstrual season (probable). The subject of 'syāt' is the embryo/child. garbha is rendered 'embryo'; 'fetus' is also possible.
lines_deva: ऊनपंचविंशतिवर्षेणोनषोडशवर्षीयामाहितो गर्भःकुक्षिस्य एव विनाशमाप्नुयादल्पायुर्बलारोग्यविभवो वा स्याद्विक्लेंद्रियो वा ऋतावाद्ये च रात्रित्रये तथा दुष्टे शुक्रार्तवहति
lines_iast: ūnapaṃcaviṃśativarṣeṇonaṣoḍaśavarṣīyāmāhito garbhaḥkukṣisya eva vināśamāpnuyādalpāyurbalārogyavibhavo vā syādvikleṃdriyo vā ṛtāvādye ca rātritraye tathā duṣṭe śukrārtavahati

hindi: वहाँ भोजन का, जो ठीक प्रकार परिणत होकर क्रम से मज्जा को प्राप्त हुआ है, सार शुक्र यानी वीर्य नाम पाता है।
english: There, the essence (sāra) of food that has been well transformed and has in order reached the marrow (majjan) obtains the name śukra (semen).
notes: Identification: śukra = semen (standard). majjan = marrow (probable; here the body tissue majjā, not a seed kernel). 'tatra' is taken as 'there/in that case'.

words.gloss: kalā (a membranous layer of the body; doctrinal term)
by striking together (saṃprahana; probably sexual union)
ghee; oil; honey (kṣaudra); any one of; colour

hindi: वह, दूध में घी और ईख के रस में गुड़ की तरह, शरीर में शुक्रधरा कला यानी झिल्लीदार परत का आश्रय लेकर समस्त अंगों में व्याप्त होने से स्थित रहता है, और विशेषकर मज्जा, मुष्क यानी वृषण और स्तनों में; हर्ष से, संप्रहन यानी आपस में टकराने से, प्रेरित होकर, हृदय के आवेश से, पिण्ड बनकर, अंग-अंग से निकलता है। वह सौम्य, स्निग्ध, भारी, श्वेत, मधु की गन्ध वाला, मधुर, पिच्छिल, बहुत, गाढ़ा, और घी, तेल या शहद में से किसी एक के रंग वाला शुक्र यानी वीर्य गर्भाधान के योग्य होता है।
english: That, like ghee in milk and jaggery in sugarcane juice, abides in the body, resting in the śukra-bearing kalā (a membranous layer), by pervading all the limbs, and especially in the marrow (majjā), the testicles (muṣka) and the breasts; stirred up by excitement, by saṃprahana (striking together), from the possession of the heart, having become a lump, it issues from limb to limb. That śukra (semen), gentle (saumya), unctuous, heavy, white, honey-scented, sweet, slimy, abundant, thick, and of the colour of any one of ghee, oil or honey, becomes fit for conception (garbhādhāna).

text_flags.why: possible: 'tat tu' (that, indeed) for the printed tatu
possible: 'kṣīre iva' (like in milk); ha/i confusion
possible: 'iva' printed as 'hava'; sarpiḥ + ikṣurase
possible: b for v, o for ā, ṃ lost

notes: No subject is named for the first sentence ('tat' neuter); it is read as the śukra of the next sentence. The similes 'kṣīre iva sarpiḥ, ikṣurase iva guḍaḥ' (ghee in milk, jaggery in sugarcane juice) rest on three corrections that are likely but not certain. kalā: a doctrinal term for a membranous layer or sheath; no modern equivalent forced. saṃprahana: literally a striking together; 'probably sexual union' is an interpretation, not certain. hṛdayāveśāt: 'from the possession (absorption) of the heart'; understood as emotional absorption, not certain. majjā here = marrow (body tissue). 'varṇa' is in the Sanskrit and is translated 'colour'. Identifications: śukra = semen (standard); muṣka = testicle (standard).
lines_deva: ततु क्षीरहव सर्पिरिक्षुरसहव गुडः शरीरे शुक्रधरां कलामाश्रित्य सर्बोगव्यापितया स्थितं विशेषतश्च मज्जमुष्कस्तनेषु हर्षोदीरितं तु संप्रहनेन हृदयावेशात्पिंडीभूतमंगादंगात्प्रवर्तते तत्सौम्यं स्निग्धं गुरु शुक्लंमधुगंधि मधुरं पिच्छिलं बहु बहलं घृततैलक्षौद्रान्यतमवर्णं च शुक्रंगर्भाधानयोग्यं भवति
lines_iast: tatu kṣīrahava sarpirikṣurasahava guḍaḥ śarīre śukradharāṃ kalāmāśritya sarbogavyāpitayā sthitaṃ viśeṣataśca majjamuṣkastaneṣu harṣodīritaṃ tu saṃprahanena hṛdayāveśātpiṃḍībhūtamaṃgādaṃgātpravartate tatsaumyaṃ snigdhaṃ guru śuklaṃmadhugaṃdhi madhuraṃ picchilaṃ bahu bahalaṃ ghṛtatailakṣaudrānyatamavarṇaṃ ca śukraṃgarbhādhānayogyaṃ bhavati

hindi: उसी प्रकार स्त्रियों का रक्त ही, हर मास गर्भकोष्ठ यानी सम्भवतः गर्भाशय को प्राप्त होकर, तीन दिन बहता हुआ, आर्तव यानी रजोधर्म का रक्त कहा जाता है।
english: Likewise, the blood itself of women, month by month, having reached the garbhakoṣṭha (probably the womb), flowing for three days, they call ārtava (menstrual blood).
notes: 'garbhakoṣṭha' = literally 'store-room (hollow) of the embryo'; modern equivalent womb/uterus (probable). 'ārtavam iti āhuḥ': they call it ārtava. 'māse māse' = every month.
lines_deva: तथा रक्तमेव च स्त्रीणां मासे मासे गर्भकोष्ठमनुप्राप्य त्र्यहं प्रवर्तमानमार्तवमित्याहुः
lines_iast: tathā raktameva ca strīṇāṃ māse māse garbhakoṣṭhamanuprāpya tryahaṃ pravartamānamārtavamityāhuḥ

words.gloss: pradara (abnormal vaginal discharge or bleeding; probable)

hindi: अतिप्रसंग से, ऋतु के अतिरिक्त समय में या ऋतु में, वही असृग्दर यानी सम्भवतः अधिक रजःस्राव, प्रदर यानी सम्भवतः योनि से असामान्य स्राव और व्यापद यानी विकार तथा रक्तयोनि नाम पाता है।
english: Through excessive continuation, whether out of season or in season, that very thing obtains the names asṛgdara (probably excessive menstrual bleeding), pradara (probably abnormal vaginal discharge or bleeding) and vyāpad (disorder), and the name raktayoni.

text_flags.why: possible: printed spacing shifted; the final ā is the first letter of asṛgdaram (tad eva + asṛgdaram)
initial a joins the previous printed token by sandhi (evāsṛg-)

notes: Reading: 'anṛtau ṛtau vā tad eva asṛgdaram pradaram vyāpadam ca raktayonisaṃjñām labhate'. The accusatives asṛgdaram, pradaram, vyāpadam and raktayoni-saṃjñām are taken as the names obtained; the exact relation is not certain. 'tad' refers back to ārtava of unit 11. Identification: asṛgdara, pradara = excessive menstrual or vaginal bleeding/discharge (probable; usage varies). raktayoni kept as a name (literally 'blood-womb').
lines_deva: अतिप्रसंगेनानृतावृतौ वातदेवा सृग्दरं प्रदरं व्यापदं च रक्तयोनिसंज्ञां लभते
lines_iast: atiprasaṃgenānṛtāvṛtau vātadevā sṛgdaraṃ pradaraṃ vyāpadaṃ ca raktayonisaṃjñāṃ labhate

hindi: उसके साधन में रक्तपित्त यानी सम्भवतः रक्तस्राव वाले विकार की चिकित्सा और गुह्य रोगों के प्रतिषेध को भी देखे।
english: In the management of that, one should look to the treatment of raktapitta (probably a bleeding disorder) and the remedy (pratiṣedha) for diseases of the private parts (guhya-roga).
notes: raktapitta kept in Sanskrit; modern equivalent a bleeding disorder (probable, not a single modern disease). guhya = private (genital) parts. 'īkṣeta' = should look to / consult.

hindi: जिनके मार्ग वात और कफ से ढके हों उनका, न बहता हुआ, पित्त बढ़ाने वाले उपचारों से वह बहता हुआ, शुक्र के साथ या शुक्र के बिना, जीवरहित, वात बढ़ाने वालों का सेवन करती हुई स्त्री का, गर्भ के लक्षण दिखाता हुआ, गुल्म वाला हो जाता है; वहाँ गुल्म की चिकित्सा को देखे।
english: Of those whose passages are covered by Vāta and Kapha, not flowing; when that flows through Pitta-increasing measures, with semen or without semen, devoid of life, of a woman who resorts to Vāta-increasing (ones), showing the signs of pregnancy, it becomes one with gulma (an abdominal lump); in that case one should look to the treatment of gulma.

text_flags.why: possible: 'aśukam' is not a word; opposite of saṃśukram 'with śukra' is aśukram 'without śukra'

notes: The sentence is loose and its syntax is not certain. The words are translated in the printed order. It appears that the blood (ārtava) of unit 11 is the unstated subject, retained and later flowing, and that what results shows signs of pregnancy and is lifeless (jīva-rahita); the reading 'gulmī bhavati' = 'becomes gulmin' (a person or thing with gulma) is not decided. gulma kept in Sanskrit; commonly an abdominal lump or mass (standard rendering).

words.gloss: Vāta; belly (vātodara: Vāta-belly, abdominal swelling from Vāta; probable)

hindi: कभी गर्भवती स्त्री में भी वातोदर यानी सम्भवतः वात से पेट का फूलना हो जाता है; वह वात को शान्त करने वालों से शान्त हो जाता है।
english: Or sometimes, in a pregnant (woman) indeed, vātodara (Vāta-belly: probably abdominal swelling from Vāta) occurs; that subsides with Vāta-pacifying (ones).
notes: 'garbhaiva' is ambiguous: garbhā eva ('a pregnant woman indeed'; taken here) or garbha eva ('the embryo itself'); garbha iva would give garbheva, so 'as if pregnant' is not read. vātodara: Vāta-belly, a swelling of the belly attributed to Vāta; modern equivalent probably abdominal distension (probable). 'vāta-aupaśamana' = Vāta-pacifying; the noun they qualify is not stated.

hindi: वही आर्तव कभी सौम्य, बृंहण यानी पुष्टि करने वाले स्वभाव के आहार और विहारों से रुका हुआ, उपद्रवरहित ही उदर को, मानो गर्भ से अधिष्ठित हो, बढ़ा देता है।
english: That very ārtava (menstrual blood), sometimes held back by gentle diets and regimens of a bulk-promoting (bṛṃhaṇa) nature, increases the belly (udara), free of complications indeed, as if occupied by an embryo.

text_flags.why: dv for dh: OCR/print confusion; vardhayati 'makes grow'

notes: Subject is ārtava; stambhita is taken with ārtava, anupadrava with udara (belly); the grouping of these adjectives is not certain. bṛṃhaṇa = bulk-promoting, nourishing (doctrinal term). 'udara' is rendered 'belly'.

hindi: जिससे मूढ़ लोग उस अगर्भिणी को गर्भिणी कहते हैं।
english: Because of which the deluded call her, who is not pregnant, pregnant.

text_flags.why: possible: the final -m and -ṇī- seem lost; agarbhīm would also scan

notes: 'yena' is taken as 'by which / because of which' (the appearance described in 16).

hindi: तब विपरीतों से या संयोग से रक्त के बहने पर गर्भ का शरीर न देखते हुए अज्ञ लोग कहते हैं कि भूतों द्वारा हर लिया गया।
english: Then, when the blood flows through contrary (ones) or by chance, not seeing the body of the embryo, the ignorant say: 'carried off by beings (bhūta)'.
notes: 'viparītaiḥ' (contrary) has no stated noun; it probably refers to the opposite measures to those in unit 16 (not certain). 'bhūta' = being, spirit; kept literal.
lines_deva: ततो विपरीतैर्यदृच्छया वाप्रवृत्ते रक्ते गर्भशरीरमपश्यंतो भूतहृतमित्यज्ञा ब्रुवते
lines_iast: tato viparītairyadṛcchayā vāpravṛtte rakte garbhaśarīramapaśyaṃto bhūtahṛtamityajñā bruvate

hindi: क्योंकि राक्षसों द्वारा ओज यानी जीवन-सार का अपहरण सम्भव है, परन्तु शरीर का नहीं, अनिष्ट होने से या असमर्थता से।
english: Since the taking away of ojas (vital essence) by rakṣas (demons) occurs, but not of the body, from undesirability or from incapacity.

text_flags.why: possible: initial a of aśakteḥ lost in the printed ād-ś

notes: Elliptical: 'apaharaṇam' (taking away) is carried over to 'of the body'. Whose undesirability or incapacity is meant is not stated. GROUPING: appears to continue the argument of unit 18 (yasmāt gives the reason).

hindi: क्योंकि इच्छा और शक्ति की प्रवृत्ति की उपलब्धि नहीं होती, और किसी के देह का मनुष्यों द्वारा अपहरण नहीं देखा जाता।
english: For there is no perception of the activity of desire and power, and the removal of anyone's body by humans is not seen.

text_flags.why: print spacing: the initial r is the visarga of the preceding word (pravṛtter upalabdhir na)
possible: its visarga (r) stands at the start of the next printed token

notes: Reading adopted on a print-spacing correction: the printed 'pravṛtte rupalabdhirna' is pravṛtter upalabdhir na (the r is the visarga of pravṛtteḥ, displaced across the space, as in unit 5); the earlier locative-dual-absolute reading is dropped. 'icchā-śaktayoḥ' is then a genitive dual dependent on pravṛtteḥ. The argument (demons act by will and power unseen; no human removal of a body is seen) is not firm, hence low confidence. GROUPING: appears to continue unit 19 (hi).
lines_deva: इच्छाशक्तयोर्हि प्रवृत्ते रुपलब्धिर्न च दृश्यते कस्यचिन्मानुषैर्देहापहारः
lines_iast: icchāśaktayorhi pravṛtte rupalabdhirna ca dṛśyate kasyacinmānuṣairdehāpahāraḥ

hindi: और यदि कुछ अत्यधिक शक्ति से युक्त लोग देखे हुए को भी लाँघकर गर्भ के शरीर को फेंकने में प्रवृत्त होते हैं, तब कैसे भला प्राप्तविशराः, जो अस्पष्ट शब्द है, अनुमानित पाठ पर, उसकी माताओं की उपेक्षा करेंगे।
english: And if some, endowed with excessive power, passing beyond even what is seen, proceed to cast off the body of the embryo, then how indeed would the prāptaviśarāḥ (unclear, on a conjectural reading) neglect its mothers?

text_flags.why: possible: visarga lost before garbhasya
the word prāptaviśarāḥ is unclear; no sure restoration; the rest tad-jananīḥ upekṣeran is clear

notes: Damaged or unclear word 'prāptaviśarāḥ' kept unsplit; it is probably an adjective or subject of 'upekṣeran' (the beings said to take the embryo?), but this is a conjecture and the translation of that part is on a conjectural reading. 'ākṣepa' = casting off or removal. 'dṛṣṭam api samullaṅghya' = literally 'even having transgressed what is seen'. The doubled tt in 'pravarttante' is normalised. GROUPING: appears to continue the argument of units 19-20.
lines_deva: यदि च दृष्टमपि समुल्लंघ्य केचिदतिशयशक्तियुक्ता गर्भस्यशरीराक्षेपे प्रवर्त्तन्ते तदा कथमिव प्राप्तविशरास्तज्जननीरुपेक्षेरन्
lines_iast: yadi ca dṛṣṭamapi samullaṃghya kecidatiśayaśaktiyuktā garbhasyaśarīrākṣepe pravarttante tadā kathamiva prāptaviśarāstajjananīrupekṣeran

words.gram: pres. part. pass. vi-√rañj, n. acc. sg.

hindi: आर्तव को फिर, जो खरगोश के रक्त और लाक्षा यानी लाख के रस के समान हो और धोने पर रंग छोड़ता जाए, शुद्ध कहते हैं।
english: Ārtava (menstrual blood), moreover, which resembles hare's blood and lākṣā (lac) juice and, when washed, loses its colour, they call pure.
notes: lākṣā = lac, the resin dye of the lac insect (standard). 'śaśarudhira-lākṣārasa' is read as a dvandva (hare's blood and lac-juice), not decided. 'virajyamāna' = losing colour (becoming decoloured).
lines_deva: आर्तवं पुनः शशरुधिरलाक्षारसोपमं धौतं च विरज्यमानं शुद्धमाहुः
lines_iast: ārtavaṃ punaḥ śaśarudhiralākṣārasopamaṃ dhautaṃ ca virajyamānaṃ śuddhamāhuḥ

words.gloss: less than; sixteen; past; seventy; years

hindi: और जैसे बाल या जीर्ण वृक्ष का पुष्प-फल, या वैसे पुष्प-फल की गन्ध उपलब्ध नहीं होती, वैसे ही सोलह वर्ष से कम या सत्तर वर्ष से अधिक बीते हुए पुरुष के शुक्रसेक आदि नहीं।
english: And just as, of a young or an old tree, the flower and fruit, or of the flower and fruit of such a kind the smell, is not found, so indeed not of a man of less than sixteen or past seventy years are the emission of semen (śukra) and the rest.
notes: Elliptical: the verb 'is found' (na upalabhyate) is carried to the first clause (puṣpaphalam) and to the last (śukrasekādayaḥ); no verb is supplied in the translations beyond what the English needs. 'na ūna-ṣoḍaśa-atīta-saptati-varṣasya' is read 'not [in a man] of less than sixteen and past seventy years'; 'ūna-ṣoḍaśa' = under sixteen, 'atīta-saptati' = past seventy. jīrṇa here = old (of a tree). śukra-seka = emission (sprinkling) of semen.
lines_deva: यथाच बालस्य जीर्णस्य वा तरोः पुष्पफलं पुष्पफलस्य वा तद्विधस्य गंधो नोपलभ्यते तथैव नोनषोडशातीतसप्ततिवर्षस्य पुंसः शुक्रसेकादयः
lines_iast: yathāca bālasya jīrṇasya vā taroḥ puṣpaphalaṃ puṣpaphalasya vā tadvidhasya gaṃdho nopalabhyate tathaiva nonaṣoḍaśātītasaptativarṣasya puṃsaḥ śukrasekādayaḥ

words.gloss: less than; twelve; past; fifty; years
rajas (menses; standard); breast milk (stanya); and the rest

hindi: और बारह वर्ष से कम या पचास वर्ष से अधिक बीते हुए वर्षों वाली स्त्री के रजस्, स्तन्य आदि।
english: And of a woman of less than twelve or past fifty years, the rajas (menses), breast milk (stanya) and the rest.

text_flags.why: possible: -aiti for -a iti (ādayaḥ iti)

notes: Elliptical: continues 23 ('na upalabhyate' carried). 'yoṣit' (nominative) beside 'varṣāyāḥ' (genitive) does not agree; the text may intend yoṣitaḥ; the printed forms are kept. The closing 'iti' marks the end of the statement. Identification: rajas = menstrual flow (standard in this sense); stanya = breast milk (standard). GROUPING: appears to complete the statement of unit 23.

hindi: अब जिस जोड़े के शुक्र और आर्तव शुद्ध हों, जो निरोग हो और परस्पर अनुरक्त हो, उस जोड़े का स्नेहन करके, विधि के अनुसार शोधन करके, आस्थापन यानी काढ़े की वस्ति और अनुवासन यानी तेल की वस्ति से उपचार करे।
english: Then, having oleated a couple whose semen (śukra) and ārtava are pure, who are free of disease and mutually attached, and having cleansed them as prescribed, one should treat them with āsthāpana (decoction enema) and anuvāsana (oil enema).

text_flags.why: possible: upasneya for upasnehya (abs. of upa-√snih); h lost

notes: 'saṃśoddhya' is printed with doubled dd; normalised to saṃśodhya. 'āsthāpana' and 'anuvāsana' are two kinds of enema (basti); āsthāpana is the decoction type and anuvāsana the oil type (both standard). The printed 'āsthāpana anuvāsanābhyām' is one dvandva instrumental dual across a printed space. The subject of 'upācaret' is unstated ('one'). 'mithuna' = couple.
lines_deva: अथ शुद्धशुक्रार्तवमरोगं मिथोऽनुरक्तं मिथुनमुपस्नेय विधिवत्संशोद्ध्यास्थापन अनुवासनाभ्यामुपाचरेत्
lines_iast: atha śuddhaśukrārtavamarogaṃ mitho'nuraktaṃ mithunamupasneya vidhivatsaṃśoddhyāsthāpana anuvāsanābhyāmupācaret

hindi: विशेष रूप से, घी और दूध वाले मधुर औषधों के संस्कारों से पुरुष को, तेल से नारी को, और पित्त बढ़ाने वाले मांसों से।
english: But especially, with preparations of sweet medicines containing ghee and milk, the man; with oil, the woman; and with Pitta-increasing meats.
notes: Elliptical: 'upācaret' of 25 is carried. How the instruments are shared between man and woman is not marked by the case endings: tailena may go with nārīm only, and pittalaiḥ māṃsaiḥ may belong to either or both. The literal order is kept. 'pittalaiḥ' = Pitta-increasing (ones); the noun it agrees with is māṃsaiḥ. GROUPING: appears to continue unit 25.
lines_deva: विशेषतस्तु घृतक्षीरवद्भिर्मधुरौषधसंस्कारैः पुरुषं तैलेन नारीं पित्तलैश्च मांसैः
lines_iast: viśeṣatastu ghṛtakṣīravadbhirmadhurauṣadhasaṃskāraiḥ puruṣaṃ tailena nārīṃ pittalaiśca māṃsaiḥ

hindi: इस प्रकार समान गुण होने से शुक्र और आर्तव पुष्ट होता है।
english: Thus indeed, by the likeness of qualities, the semen (śukra) and ārtava are nourished.
notes: 'samāna-guṇatā' = state of having similar qualities (doctrine of like increasing like). 'āpyāyate' = is nourished, increased.

words.gloss: Vāta; Pitta; Śleṣma (Kapha); corpse; smelling; knot; pus; wasted; urine; faeces; semens (retas; standard)

hindi: वात, पित्त, श्लेष्मा, कुणपगन्धि, ग्रन्थि, पूय, क्षीण, मूत्र-पुरीष वाले रेतस् यानी वीर्य तो बीजहीन होते हैं।
english: The semens (retas) that are Vāta, Pitta, Śleṣma (Kapha), corpse-smelling, knot, pus, wasted, urine-and-faeces, however, are seedless (abīja).
notes: The long compound is read as a list of eight kinds of faulty semen: Vāta, Pitta, Śleṣma, kuṇapa-gandhi, granthi, pūya, kṣīṇa, mūtra-purīṣa, all qualifying 'retāṃsi'; it appears that the following units 29-37 treat these in turn (29 Vāta, 30 Pitta, 31 Śleṣma, 32 blood, 33 Vāta-Śleṣma, 34 Pitta-Śleṣma, 35 Vāta-Pitta, 37 sannipāta), but the pairing is not stated here. 'kuṇapa-gandhi' is read as one member (corpse-smelling), 'mūtra-purīṣa' as one member. 'abīja' = seedless, i.e. not a fertile seed (probable sense: not capable of conception).

hindi: उनमें पतला, रूखा, झागदार, लालिमायुक्त, थोड़ा, टूटा हुआ, पीड़ा सहित, और देर से, वात के कारण निकलता है।
english: Among these: thin, rough, frothy, reddish, scanty, interrupted, with pain, and after a long time it is discharged, by Vāta.
notes: The unstated subject (the semen) is shown only by the neuter adjectives. 'niṣicyate' = is poured out, discharged. 'aruṇa' = reddish (dawn colour).
lines_deva: तत्र तनु रूक्षं फेनिलमरुणमल्पं विच्छिन्नं सरुजं चिराच्च निषिच्यते वातेन
lines_iast: tatra tanu rūkṣaṃ phenilamaruṇamalpaṃ vicchinnaṃ sarujaṃ cirācca niṣicyate vātena

hindi: थोड़ा पीला, पिच्छिलता रहित, या नीला, दहद्विष जो अस्पष्ट है, पित्त के कारण निकलता है। मज्जा से मिला हुआ, बहुत, बँधा हुआ, और पानी में कुछ डूबता है, श्लेष्मा के कारण।
english: Slightly yellow, non-slimy, or blue, dahadviṣa (unclear), it issues by Pitta. Mixed with marrow (majjā), abundant, bound, and it sinks somewhat in water, by Śleṣma (Kapha).

text_flags.why: possible: stray final a (apicchilama) before nīlam; it may instead be the a of anīlam, but 'or not blue' does not suit
possible: unclear; 'dahat' (burning) is likely, 'viṣa' could be poison; no sure restoration

notes: [02.01.30] Unclear word 'dahadviṣa' kept unsplit and untranslated; a conjectural reading would be 'burning (like) poison'. The stray 'a' after apicchilam is read as a printing slip, so that nīlam vā = 'or blue'; the other reading (apicchilam anīlam vā) is possible. The doubled tt in 'pravarttate' is normalised. [02.01.31] Elliptical: the semen and its issuing are understood from 29-30. majja here = marrow, the body tissue; 'mixed with marrow' is the literal rendering and its sense is not explained by the text. 'ambhasi' = in water.
lines_deva: किंचित्पीतमपिच्छिलम नीलं वा दहद्विष प्रवर्त्तते पित्तेन
मज्जोपसंसृष्टंप्रभूतं विबद्धं चांभसि च किंचिन्मज्जति श्लेष्मणा
lines_iast: kiṃcitpītamapicchilama nīlaṃ vā dahadviṣa pravarttate pittena
majjopasaṃsṛṣṭaṃprabhūtaṃ vibaddhaṃ cāṃbhasi ca kiṃcinmajjati śleṣmaṇā

hindi: शव की गन्ध वाला, थोड़ा, रक्त के कारण।
english: Corpse-smelling, scanty, by blood.
notes: Elliptical: verb and subject carried from 29-31. 'rakta' = blood, here the agent as Vāta, Pitta and Śleṣma were in 29-31; it is not called a doṣa in the line.

hindi: ग्रन्थि बना हुआ, वात और श्लेष्मा के कारण।
english: Become a knot (granthi), by Vāta and Śleṣma (Kapha).
notes: Elliptical: continues the list of 28-32. GROUPING: the units 32-37 are short phrases that appear to continue one sentence from unit 29.

hindi: सड़े हुए पूय के समान, पित्त और श्लेष्मा के कारण।
english: Resembling foul pus, by Pitta and Śleṣma (Kapha).
notes: 'pūti' = foul, putrid; 'nibha' = resembling. Elliptical, as in 33.

hindi: क्षीण, वात और पित्त के कारण।
english: Wasted (kṣīṇa), by Vāta and Pitta.
notes: Elliptical, as in 33. 'kṣīṇa' = wasted, depleted, diminished.

hindi: वह साधन सहित पहले कहा जा चुका है।
english: That has been stated before, with its treatment.
notes: 'tat' is unspecified; it probably refers to the treatment of the conditions just listed, stated earlier in the work (not certain which place). 'sādhana' here = treatment (remedy).

words.gloss: by sannipāta (the three doṣas together; doctrinal term)

hindi: मूत्र और मल की गन्ध वाला, सन्निपात यानी तीनों दोषों के एक साथ होने के कारण।
english: Smelling of urine and faeces, by sannipāta (the three doṣas together).
notes: Elliptical, as in 33. sannipāta: a doctrinal term for the combination of all three doṣas; no modern equivalent forced. 'purīṣa' = faeces (stool).

hindi: आर्तव भी, शुक्र के दोषों से मिला हुआ, बीजहीन ही होता है।
english: The ārtava (menstrual blood) also, when joined with the faults (doṣa) of śukra (semen), is itself seedless.
notes: 'doṣa' here = fault (flaw) of śukra, as in the eight kinds listed in 28, not the humour. 'eva' = indeed, only. No verb is stated; the copula is understood.

hindi: उसका लक्षण और नाम पहले के समान।
english: Its sign and name as before.
notes: Elliptical: no verb stated. 'tasya' refers to the ārtava of 38. 'pūrvavat' = as before, i.e. as for śukra in 29-37 (not certain how far).

hindi: उनमें कुणप, ग्रन्थि, पूय और क्षीण रेतस् यानी वीर्य कठिनाई से साध्य हैं। परन्तु मूत्र-पुरीष वाला शुक्र और आर्तव असाध्य है, अथवा कुणप, ग्रन्थि या पूय आर्तव।
english: Among these, the corpse-smelling, knot, pus and wasted semens (retas) are curable with difficulty. But the urine-and-faeces śukra and ārtava is incurable, or the kuṇapa, granthi or pūya ārtava.
notes: [02.01.40] 'kṛcchra-sādhana' = treatable only with difficulty. No verb stated; the copula is understood. 'kuṇapa' here stands for kuṇapa-gandhi of 28. [02.01.41] Compound structure is not marked: 'mūtra-purīṣa-śukra-ārtavam' is read as the urine-faeces kind of semen and of ārtava; 'kuṇapa-granthi-pūya-ārtavam' as the kuṇapa, granthi or pūya kind of ārtava. 'asādhya' = not to be accomplished, incurable.

hindi: उनमें पहले तीन शुक्र और आर्तव के दोषों को, प्रत्येक को अपने दोष के साधन से उपचार करे।
english: Among these, the first three faults of śukra (semen) and ārtava one should treat, each according to its own, with the treatment of the doṣa.
notes: 'ādyān trīn' = the first three (kinds) of the list in 28: presumably Vāta, Pitta and Śleṣma. 'śukrārtavadoṣān' = faults of śukra and ārtava (fault, not humour); 'doṣasādhanena' is read as the treatment of the (corresponding) doṣa, humour, which makes the logic of 'each according to its own'; the two senses of doṣa are not separated by the text. Subject of 'sādhayet' unstated ('one').

hindi: और गुह्य के प्रतिषेध से, दोनों को भी।
english: And with the remedy for the private parts (guhya-pratiṣedha), also both.
notes: GROUPING: this appears to continue unit 42 (the verb 'sādhayet' is carried over). 'ubhayān' (masculine plural 'both') is not explained by the line; it presumably refers to the two kinds of faults, those of śukra and of ārtava, but this is not stated. 'guhya' = the private (genital) parts.

words.gloss: sukta (a sour fermented liquid); saindhava (rock salt; standard); fruit; sour; cooked
barley (yava, Hordeum vulgare; standard); kṣāra; addition (prativāpa)

hindi: वातिक शुक्रदोष में सुक्त, सैन्धव यानी सेंधा नमक और खट्टे फल के साथ पकाया हुआ, यव के क्षार के प्रतिवाप सहित घी का पान।
english: In the Vāta-type fault (doṣa) of semen (śukra): drinking of ghee cooked with sukta, saindhava (rock salt) and sour fruit, with yava-kṣāra (kṣāra of barley) as the addition (prativāpa).
notes: Start of the treatment list for faults of śukra (semen) and ārtava. Parse of 'suktasaindhavaphalāmla' as three items (sukta, saindhava, sour fruit) is the plainer reading; 'phalāmla' could also be read as one sour fruit; 'sukta' is a sour fermented liquid (vinegar-like), not enriched further. 'siddha' agrees with sarpiḥ (ghee), which is only named in the last word. Prativāpa = a substance added to the preparation; the text gives no dose or stage. Identifications: saindhava = rock salt (standard); yava = barley, Hordeum vulgare (standard). Verb: none, a noun phrase ('drinking of ghee'). doṣa here is 'fault' of the semen. The printed internal ṃ in 'saiṃdhava' is the print's way of writing n.

words.gloss: bilva (bael, Aegle marmelos; standard); vidārī (Pueraria tuberosa, vidārīkanda; probable); milk; joined with
madhuka (licorice, Glycyrrhiza glabra; probable); bhadradāru (deodar, Cedrus deodara; probable); cooked

hindi: बिल्व यानी बेल, विदारी यानी सम्भवतः विदारीकन्द और दूध से युक्त आस्थापन यानी काढ़े की बस्ति। मधुक यानी सम्भवतः मुलेठी और भद्रदारु यानी सम्भवतः देवदारु के साथ पकाया हुआ तेल, अनुवासन यानी तेल की बस्ति।
english: Āsthāpana (decoction enema) joined with bilva (bael), vidārī (probably Indian kudzu, Pueraria tuberosa) and milk. Oil cooked with madhuka (probably licorice) and bhadradāru (probably deodar), as anuvāsana (oil enema).

text_flags.why: possible: 'āsthapana' has a short a; the word is āsthāpana (long ā), as printed in units 50 and 55

notes: [02.01.45] Elliptical noun phrase; the verb of administering is not stated, and none is supplied. Identifications: bilva = Aegle marmelos, bael (standard); vidārī = Pueraria tuberosa (probable; the name is also applied to other tubers). Āsthāpana is an enema with decoction (standard). The Hindi gloss 'बस्ति' is the medical enema, not the bladder. [02.01.46] Elliptical (no verb); the previous unit's therapy list continues. Identifications: madhuka = licorice, Glycyrrhiza glabra (probable; the name madhuka is also used for Madhuca trees, see unit 61); bhadradāru = Cedrus deodara, deodar, usually identified with devadāru (probable). 'tailam anuvāsanam' read as 'oil, (as) anuvāsana'.

words.gloss: milk; kulīra (crab, probable; could be a plant name); juice (rasa); cooked
uttarabasti (injection through the urinary or genital passage; standard)

hindi: दूध और कुलीर यानी सम्भवतः केकड़े के रस से पकाया हुआ तेल, उत्तरबस्ति यानी मूत्रमार्ग या योनि से दी जाने वाली बस्ति।
english: Oil cooked with milk and the juice (rasa) of kulīra (probably crab), as uttarabasti (injection through the urinary or genital passage).

text_flags.why: possible: 'rasarasa' reads as a doubled 'rasa' (dittography); one 'rasa' gives the sense 'milk, crab-juice, cooked'

notes: Elliptical (no verb). The doubled 'rasa' is taken as a print doubling; if both stand, the second rasa could be read as a further 'juice', but the sense is not changed. kulīra is read as 'crab' (standard); it can also be a plant name in some lists, so this is not certain. Uttarabasti is given through the urinary passage (man) or the genital passage (woman); the text gives no route here.

words.gloss: kāṇḍekṣu (a kind of cane; identity disputed); śvadaṃṣṭrā (puncture vine, Tribulus terrestris; standard); guḍūcī (Tinospora cordifolia; standard); cooked

hindi: पैत्तिक में काण्डेक्षु, श्वदंष्ट्रा यानी गोखरू और गुडूची यानी गिलोय के साथ पकाया हुआ, मूर्वा और मधुक के प्रतिवाप सहित घी का पान।
english: In the Pitta-type (one): drinking of ghee cooked with kāṇḍekṣu, śvadaṃṣṭrā (puncture vine) and guḍūcī (Tinospora cordifolia), with mūrvā and madhuka as the addition (pratīvāpa).

text_flags.why: possible: the second ṃ after e is not needed; the word kāṇḍa-ikṣu gives kāṇḍekṣu

notes: 'śukradoṣe' is understood from unit 44. Identifications: kāṇḍekṣu = a cane (ikṣu) of kāṇḍa kind, not identified here (disputed); śvadaṃṣṭrā = gokṣura, Tribulus terrestris (standard); guḍūcī = Tinospora cordifolia (standard); mūrvā = Marsdenia tenacissima (disputed). 'pratīvāpa' is the same as prativāpa of unit 44 (long ī as printed). The last token joins two words without a space; the printed ṃ inside is a print habit.

hindi: त्रिवृत् यानी निशोथ का चूर्ण, घी सहित, विरेचन है।
english: Powder of trivṛt (turpeth) with ghee is the purgation (virecana).

text_flags.why: possible: the colon stands for the visarga (ḥ) in the print

notes: The colon in the print is read as visarga; the Devanagari has ':' too. virekaḥ is masculine (virecana, purgation). The text says 'is' by juxtaposition; no verb in the Sanskrit, and the English 'is' is only a natural rendering of the nominal sentence.

words.gloss: payasyā (identity disputed); śrīparṇī (Gmelina arborea; probable); cooked

hindi: पयस्या और श्रीपर्णी यानी सम्भवतः गम्भारी के साथ पकाया हुआ, दूध से युक्त आस्थापन।
english: Āsthāpana (decoction enema) cooked with payasyā and śrīparṇī (probably gambhārī, Gmelina arborea), joined with milk.
notes: Elliptical. payasyā is variously identified (identity disputed; not enriched). śrīparṇī = Gmelina arborea, gambhārī (probable). 'siddha' and 'yukta' both qualify āsthāpana.

hindi: मधुक और मुद्गपर्णी यानी सम्भवतः मुँगवन के साथ पकाया हुआ तेल, अनुवासन और उत्तरबस्ति भी।
english: Oil cooked with madhuka and mudgaparṇī (probably Phaseolus trilobus), as anuvāsana (oil enema) and as uttarabasti.
notes: Elliptical. mudgaparṇī = Phaseolus trilobus (Vigna trilobata) (probable).

words.gloss: pāṣāṇabhedaka (Bergenia ligulata; probable); aśmantaka (identity disputed); āmalaka (emblic myrobalan, Phyllanthus emblica; standard); decoction (kvātha); cooked
pippalī (long pepper, Piper longum; standard); madhuka; powder; addition

hindi: श्लैष्मिक में पाषाणभेदक यानी सम्भवतः पखानभेद, अश्मन्तक और आमलक यानी आँवला के क्वाथ में पकाया हुआ, पिप्पली यानी पीपर और मधुक के चूर्ण के प्रतिवाप सहित घी का पान।
english: In the Kapha-type (one): drinking of ghee cooked with a decoction (kvātha) of pāṣāṇabhedaka (probably pāṣāṇabheda, Bergenia ligulata), aśmantaka and āmalaka (emblic myrobalan), with powder of pippalī (long pepper) and madhuka as the addition.
notes: Printed 'bhedakāśmaṃtaka' is read as bhedaka + aśmantaka by sandhi (a+a=ā). Identifications: pāṣāṇabhedaka = pāṣāṇabheda, Bergenia ligulata (probable; other plants also called pāṣāṇabheda); aśmantaka = identity disputed (Bauhinia species or a fig have been proposed), not enriched in the translation; āmalaka = Phyllanthus emblica (standard); pippalī = Piper longum (standard). Hindi 'कफज' for ślaiṣmika (Kapha-type).

hindi: मदनफल यानी मैनफल का काढ़ा वमन यानी उल्टी कराना है।
english: A decoction of madanaphala (Randia dumetorum) as vamana (emesis).
notes: Nominal sentence; no verb. kaṣāya = decoction (preparation sense). madanaphala = fruit of madana, Randia dumetorum (standard), Hindi मैनफल.

words.gloss: dantī (Baliospermum montanum; probable); viḍaṅga (Embelia ribes; standard); powder
rājavṛkṣa (Cassia fistula; standard); madanaphala; decoction; thick, strong

hindi: दन्ती यानी सम्भवतः दन्तीमूल और विडंग यानी वायविडंग का चूर्ण, तेल से चाटा गया, विरेचन है। राजवृक्ष यानी अमलतास और मदनफल के काढ़े से प्रगाढ़ आस्थापन।
english: The powder of dantī (probably Baliospermum montanum) and viḍaṅga (Embelia ribes), licked with oil, is the purgation (virecana). Āsthāpana (decoction enema) strong or thick (pragāḍha) with a decoction of rājavṛkṣa (Cassia fistula) and madanaphala.
notes: [02.01.54] 'taila-līḍha' = licked with oil. dantī = Baliospermum montanum (probable); viḍaṅga = Embelia ribes (standard). [02.01.55] Elliptical. pragāḍha = thick / strong / dense; 'strong with the decoction' is the plain reading. rājavṛkṣa = Cassia fistula (standard); the text does not say which part. Whether 'phala' (fruit) goes with both names or only madana is not decided; the compound is read as rājavṛkṣa + madanaphala.

hindi: मधुक और पिप्पली के साथ पकाया हुआ तेल, अनुवासन और उत्तरबस्ति भी। वातज आर्तव के दोष में भी भार्गी यानी भारंगी और भद्रदारु यानी सम्भवतः देवदारु के साथ पकाए हुए घी का पान।
english: Oil cooked with madhuka and pippalī (long pepper), as anuvāsana and as uttarabasti. In the Vāta-type fault of ārtava (menstrual blood) also: drinking of ghee cooked with bhārgī (Clerodendrum serratum) and bhadradāru (probably deodar).
notes: GROUPING: the unit appears to join two statements. The first part (oil with madhuka and pippalī as anuvāsana and uttarabasti) appears to continue the Kapha-type therapies of 52-55; the second part ('vātaje api ārtavadoṣe …') starts the ārtava (menstrual blood) faults. The print omits the space in 'ārtavadoṣebhārgī…' (read as ārtavadoṣe + bhārgī). 'api' may mean that the Vāta-type of ārtava is treated 'also' like the earlier cases. Identification: bhārgī = Clerodendrum serratum (standard).

words.gloss: unclear (damaged compound, begins like kāśmarya and kṣudrasahā, ends 'cooked')

hindi: अथवा, अनुमानित पाठ पर, काश्मर्य, क्षुद्रसहा और एक अस्पष्ट शब्द के साथ पकाया हुआ दूध। मधुक और शृगालविन्ना के कल्क में, दूध और घी के साथ संयुक्त।
english: Or milk cooked with kāśmarya, kṣudrasahā and an unclear word, on a conjectural reading. In a paste (kalka) of madhuka and śṛgālavinnā, combined with milk and ghee.

text_flags.why: damaged: 'sūi' is not a word; the middle is unrestorable (a drug name may stand there), and 'kṣudrasahā' is itself doubtful
possible: 'sahitam' is neuter nominative/accusative, so 'kalkam' (paste combined with milk and ghee) fits better than the locative

notes: [02.01.57] Damaged print: the printed word is kept unsplit. The beginning kāśmarya (Gmelina arborea, gambhārī; standard) and kṣudrasahā (a drug name, identity disputed) is a reading only; the part 'sūi' is unclear and nothing is built on it. Translation therefore given on a conjectural reading, and the grammar (milk cooked with the drugs) is also conjectural. [02.01.58] As printed, kalke is locative; the neuter 'sahitam' suggests kalkam. Both readings are literal-possible; the translation follows the printed locative. Elliptical. śṛgālavinnā: identity disputed (Pseudarthria viscida has been proposed), not enriched in the translation.

words.gloss: priyaṅgu (Callicarpa macrophylla; probable); tila (sesame, Sesamum indicum; standard); paste

hindi: अथवा प्रियंगु यानी सम्भवतः फूलप्रियंगु और तिल का कल्क योनि में धारण करे। सरल यानी सम्भवतः चीड़ और मुद्गपर्णी का काढ़ा प्रक्षालन है।
english: Or one should hold a paste (kalka) of priyaṅgu (probably Callicarpa macrophylla) and tila (sesame) in the yoni (vagina). A decoction of sarala (probably Pinus roxburghii) and mudgaparṇī as the wash (prakṣālana).
notes: [02.01.59] Identifications: priyaṅgu = Callicarpa macrophylla (probable; the name is also used for other plants); tila = Sesamum indicum (standard). 'kalka' is taken as masculine here. [02.01.60] Nominal sentence. sarala = Pinus roxburghii, chir pine (probable). kaṣāya = decoction. Wash presumably of the yoni, from the preceding unit, but the text does not say.

words.gloss: kākolī (identity disputed); pair; vidārī; root; decoction
utpala (blue lotus, Nymphaea; probable); padmaka (Prunus cerasoides; probable); decoction
madhuka (Madhuca tree is possible here); flower; kāśmarya (Gmelina arborea; standard); fruit; decoction
vāsa (probably vāsā, Adhatoda vasica; probable, short a as printed); sugar (śarkarā)

hindi: पित्तज में काकोली के जोड़े और विदारी की जड़ का क्वाथ, उत्पल और पद्मक का क्वाथ, मधुक के फूल और काश्मर्य के फल का क्वाथ, वास यानी सम्भवतः अडूसा और शर्करा सहित पीए।
english: In the Pitta-type (one) one should drink the decoction of the pair of kākolī and the root of vidārī, the decoction of utpala and padmaka, and the decoction of the flower of madhuka and the fruit of kāśmarya, with vāsa (probably Adhatoda vasica) and sugar.
notes: Identifications: kākolī = identity disputed (a Himalayan tuber, with its pair kṣīrakākolī, is proposed), not enriched; utpala = blue lotus (probable); padmaka = Prunus cerasoides (probable); vāsa = Adhatoda vasica (standard). The decoction kvātha is repeated three times; whether 'with vāsa and sugar' applies to one or all three is not decided by the Sanskrit. 'madhuka-puṣpa': the flower suggests the madhuka tree (Madhuca), not licorice. Taken as 'flower of madhuka, fruit of kāśmarya'; the alternative 'madhuka; flower and fruit of kāśmarya' is possible. 'vāsa' is printed with short a; read as vāsā (probable, not certain). 'with' before vāsa and sugar is a supplied preposition for an accusative compound; it could also be two more items drunk.

hindi: अथवा श्वेत चन्दन का क्वाथ, शहद सहित।
english: Or a decoction of white sandalwood (śveta-candana, probably Santalum album), with honey.
notes: Elliptical; 'pibet' is not stated here. śveta-candana = white sandalwood, Santalum album (probable). kṣaudra = honey (standard).

words.gloss: dhava (Anogeissus latifolia; probable); dhātakī (Woodfordia fruticosa; standard); paste

hindi: अथवा धव यानी सम्भवतः धौ और धातकी यानी धाय का कल्क।
english: Or a paste (kalka) of dhava (probably Anogeissus latifolia) and dhātakī (Woodfordia fruticosa).
notes: Elliptical. dhava = Anogeissus latifolia (probable); dhātakī = Woodfordia fruticosa (standard); the part used is not named.

words.gloss: madhuka; madhurasā (identity disputed); mṛdvīkā (grape or raisin, Vitis vinifera; standard); paste

hindi: अथवा घी के साथ मधुक, मधुरसा और मृद्वीका यानी मुनक्का का कल्क।
english: Or, with ghee, a paste (kalka) of madhuka, madhurasā and mṛdvīkā (grape or raisin).
notes: Elliptical. madhurasā: identity disputed (several plants carry the name), not enriched. mṛdvīkā = grape or raisin, Vitis vinifera (standard).

words.gloss: śamyāka (probably Cassia fistula; disputed); gavākṣī (Citrullus colocynthis; probable); milk

hindi: शम्याक, गवाक्षी यानी सम्भवतः इन्द्रायण और दूध विरेचन है।
english: Śamyāka, gavākṣī (probably Citrullus colocynthis) and milk are the purgation (virecana).
notes: Nominal sentence. The compound can be read as a list 'śamyāka, gavākṣī and milk' (taken here) or as 'milk (or latex, kṣīra) of śamyāka and gavākṣī'. Identifications: śamyāka = probably Cassia fistula (disputed; another tree is also proposed); gavākṣī = Citrullus colocynthis (probable).

hindi: चन्दन और पयस्या का कल्क योनि में धारण करे।
english: One should hold a paste (kalka) of candana (sandalwood) and payasyā in the yoni (vagina).
notes: candana: the text does not say white or red (compare unit 62). payasyā identity disputed (see 50).

words.gloss: gairika (red ochre; standard); ariṣṭa (probably neem, Azadirachta indica; disputed); decoction

hindi: गैरिक यानी लाल गेरू और अरिष्ट यानी सम्भवतः नीम का काढ़ा प्रक्षालन है।
english: A decoction of gairika (red ochre) and ariṣṭa (probably neem) as the wash (prakṣālana).
notes: Nominal sentence. gairika is a mineral (red ochre), so 'decoction' of it is literal as the print says; the sense may be a decoction of ariṣṭa with gairika. ariṣṭa = probably neem (disputed; soapnut, ariṣṭaka, is also proposed).

words.gloss: kuṭaja (Holarrhena antidysenterica; standard); kaṭukā (Picrorhiza kurroa; probable); aśvagandhā (Withania somnifera; standard); decoction
unclear (damaged; begins like kṣīrivṛkṣa, milk-trees; ends like a decoction)

english: In the Kapha-type (one) one should drink a decoction of kuṭaja (Holarrhena antidysenterica), kaṭukā (probably Picrorhiza kurroa) and aśvagandhā (Withania somnifera). Or, with honey (mākṣika), on a conjectural reading a decoction relating to the milk-trees (kṣīrivṛkṣa); the printed word is unclear.

The avagraha printed after kaṭukā- is a print habit (kaṭukā + aśvagandhā), not an elision. [02.01.69] Damaged print: kept unsplit. 'kṣīrivṛkṣa' = trees with milky latex (the fig group, probable); the rest is not restorable and nothing is built on it. samākṣika = with honey (mākṣika means honey; a mineral of that name is also known, so honey is the plain sense).

hindi: अथवा इन्हीं का चूर्ण शहद और घी के साथ चाटे।
english: Or one should lick the powder of just these, with honey and ghee.

notes: 'eteṣām' refers to the drugs of the preceding Kapha-type formulas (not stated which). The dual instrumental 'madhughṛtābhyām' means with honey and ghee; no proportions are given.

hindi: मदनफल के काढ़े से वमन।
english: Vamana (emesis) with a decoction of madanaphala.
notes: Elliptical; no verb. See unit 53 for the identification of madanaphala.

hindi: और उसी का कल्क योनि में धारण करे।
english: And one should hold just its paste in the yoni (vagina).
notes: 'tat' refers to madanaphala of unit 71 (the nearest drug); this is the plain reading.

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर, रोधार्तिदुक नामक अस्पष्ट पद का काढ़ा प्रक्षालन है, अथवा बकरे और भेड़ का मूत्र।
english: On a conjectural reading, a decoction of the unclear compound rodhārtiduka- as the wash (prakṣālana), or the urine of goat and sheep.

The urine is named without any condition. Possible reading (not adopted): rodhra (lodhra) + tinduka, a decoction of two drugs; nothing is built on it.

unclear (damaged; possibly madanādibhiḥ, 'with madana and the like')

hindi: कुणप-रेतस् यानी सम्भवतः शव जैसी गन्ध वाले शुक्र में धातकी के फूल, खदिर यानी खैर, अर्जुन और दाडिम यानी अनार के साथ पकाया हुआ, अथवा अनुमानित पाठ पर मदन आदि के साथ पकाया हुआ घी पिलाए।
english: In kuṇapa-retas (probably semen of a corpse-like smell), one should make him drink ghee cooked with dhātakī flowers, khadira (Acacia catechu), arjuna (Terminalia arjuna) and dāḍima (pomegranate), or, on a conjectural reading, with madana and the like.

hindi: ग्रन्थि-रेतस् यानी गाँठ वाले शुक्र में पाषाणभिद् यानी सम्भवतः पखानभेद से, अथवा पलाश यानी ढाक की भस्म से। पूय-रेतस् यानी पीब वाले शुक्र में परूषक यानी फालसा आदि और न्यग्रोध यानी बरगद आदि, इन दोनों से।
english: In granthi-retas (semen with knots or lumps): with pāṣāṇabhid (probably Bergenia ligulata), or with the ash of palāśa (Butea monosperma). In pūya-retas (semen with pus): with the two (groups) beginning with parūṣaka (phalsa, Grewia asiatica) and beginning with nyagrodha (banyan, Ficus benghalensis).
notes: [02.01.75] Elliptical: the verb and the nature of the preparation are not stated (the verb of unit 74 may be carried over; none supplied). pāṣāṇabhid = pāṣāṇabheda (Bergenia ligulata, probable, see 52). palāśa = Butea monosperma (standard). 'granthi-retas' = semen with granthi (knot / lump), the text gives no further description. [02.01.76] Elliptical; the verb and the form of use (decoction, paste, etc.) are not stated. The dual 'ādibhyām' is read as the two groups parūṣakādi and nyagrodhādi (named drug groups); the members of the groups are not given here and are not supplied. parūṣaka = Grewia asiatica (standard); nyagrodha = Ficus benghalensis (standard). The first 'ādi' is in compound form, so the dual ending is read once on the second.

or else (athavā, with the next word)

hindi: मूत्र-पुरीष-रेतस् यानी सम्भवतः मूत्र और मल वाले शुक्र में, जो वायु से अत्यन्त विकृत हुआ है, हींग, अनुमानित पाठ पर उशीर यानी सम्भवतः खस, और चित्रक यानी चीता से; अथवा चित्रक, वितुन्नक, प्रियंगु, हींग, समंगा और मृणाल के साथ पकाया हुआ, एला यानी सम्भवतः छोटी इलायची और मोच के चूर्ण के प्रतिवाप सहित।
english: In mūtra-purīṣa-retas (probably semen with urine and feces) greatly altered by Vāyu (wind): with hiṅgu, uśīra (probably vetiver, on a conjectural reading of the printed śīra) and citraka (leadwort); or the (one) cooked with citraka, vitunnaka, priyaṅgu, hiṅgu, samaṅgā and mṛṇāla (lotus stalk), with the powder of elā (probably small cardamom) and moca as the addition.

text_flags.why: possible: hiṅgu + uśīra gives hiṅgūśīra with long ū; the print has a short u; 'śīra' alone has no sense here

notes: Long, elliptical unit; no verb. 'mūtra-purīṣa-retas' is read as semen marked by urine and feces (probable; the exact sense is not given). 'vāyunā' = by Vāyu, the wind (Vāta). The first list (hiṅgu, uśīra, citraka) is instrumental plural and the second list is 'cooked' (siddha) with a powder as addition; the Sanskrit does not name what is cooked (supplied as 'the (one)'). citraka and hiṅgu occur in both lists as printed. Identifications: hiṅgu = Ferula assa-foetida (standard); uśīra = Vetiveria zizanioides (probable, depends on the typo reading); citraka = Plumbago zeylanica (standard); vitunnaka and samaṅgā = identity disputed, not enriched; mṛṇāla = lotus stalk (standard); elā = small cardamom (probable); moca = identity disputed (banana or a gum of the silk-cotton tree have been proposed). The printed 'mocacūrṇa' is read as 'moca' + 'cūrṇa' (mocā-cūrṇa possible).

words.gloss: pāṭhā (Cissampelos pareira; probable); trikaṇṭaka (probably Tribulus terrestris, as for śvadaṃṣṭrā; probable); vṛkṣaka (probably kuṭaja; probable); decoction

hindi: उसी प्रकार ग्रन्थि वाले आर्तव में पाठा, त्रिकण्टक यानी सम्भवतः गोखरू और वृक्षक यानी सम्भवतः कुटज का क्वाथ।
english: Likewise, in granthi-ārtava (menstrual blood with knots or lumps): a decoction of pāṭhā (probably Cissampelos pareira), trikaṇṭaka (probably Tribulus terrestris) and vṛkṣaka (probably kuṭaja, Holarrhena antidysenterica).
notes: Elliptical; the verb (pibet of unit 79) is not stated here and none is supplied. Identifications: pāṭhā = Cissampelos pareira (probable); trikaṇṭaka = Tribulus terrestris (probable, the same plant as śvadaṃṣṭrā); vṛkṣaka = kuṭaja, Holarrhena antidysenterica (probable). The part used of each is not stated.

words.gloss: triphalā (the three myrobalans; standard); paste; decoction
holding, retaining (dhāraṇa); sipping, rinsing the mouth (ācamana)

hindi: सम्भवतः शव जैसी गन्ध और पीब वाले आर्तव में चन्दन का क्वाथ पीए। और यहाँ त्रिफला यानी हरड़, बहेड़ा और आँवला का कल्क और क्वाथ, धारण और आचमन।
english: In kuṇapa-pūya-ārtava (menstrual blood with a corpse-like smell and pus, probably), one should drink a decoction of candana. And here the paste and the decoction of triphalā (the three myrobalans), the holding (dhāraṇa) and the sipping or rinsing (ācamana).
notes: 'kuṇapa-pūya' is read as corpse-like and pus (the understanding of kuṇapa as smell is probable, see unit 74). The last clause is a nominal sentence of two duals: paste and decoction, holding and rinsing; the text does not say which goes with which (paste for holding and decoction for rinsing is the natural order), and no verb is supplied. triphalā = the three myrobalans: harītakī, bibhītaka, āmalaka (standard). ācamana is primarily 'sipping' (also rinsing the mouth), not the yoni wash (prakṣālana of 60, 67, 73); the pairing of the two duals (paste:holding, decoction:sipping) is natural but not stated, and is not claimed.
lines_deva: कुणपपूयार्तवे चंदनक्वाथं पिबेत् त्रिफलाकल्कक्वाथौ चात्र धारणाचमने

hindi: और शुक्र तथा आर्तव के सभी दोषों में स्त्री और पुरुष दोनों का स्नेह यानी तेल या वसा आदि कर्मों से, विशेष रूप से उत्तरबस्तियों से, बार बार उपचार करे।
english: And in all faults (doṣa) of semen and ārtava, one should treat the woman and the man again and again with the actions beginning with sneha (oil, fat), especially with uttarabasti injections.
notes: 'sarveṣuca' is printed without a space (sarveṣu ca). 'punaḥ punaḥ' = again and again; the first 'punaḥ' is joined to 'uttarabastibhiḥ'. 'strī-puṃsau' is a dual: the woman and the man, both. 'snehādi-karma' = the actions beginning with oleation (sneha); the list is not given.

words.gloss: each according to its own, as suited

hindi: और जिसके लिए जो उचित हो, योनि में कल्कों और पिचुओं यानी रूई के फाहों से।
english: And in the yoni (vagina), as suited to each, with pastes (kalka) and with picu (cotton-wool wads).
notes: GROUPING: the unit appears to continue unit 80 (the verb 'upācaret' is carried over; none supplied). picu = a wad or swab of cotton (standard).

hindi: इस प्रकार जिन दोनों के शुक्र और आर्तव शुद्ध हों, वे पहले कही गई विधि का पालन करें। ऋतु तो दृष्ट आर्तव वाला और बारह रात तक होता है।
english: In this way, the two whose semen and ārtava are purified should follow the procedure (vidhi) stated earlier. The ṛtu (season), however, is that with ārtava seen, and it lasts twelve nights.
notes: [02.01.82] 'iti' here closes the preceding statement and is not translated. 'pūrvoktam' is masculine accusative in the print; vidhim is masculine, so it agrees. 'The two' are the man and the woman of unit 80. [02.01.83] Reading: 'ṛtuḥ dṛṣṭārtavaḥ dvādaśarātram bhavati', 'the ṛtu is one with visible ārtava, for twelve nights'. The sense of ṛtu is the woman's season for conception (probable); not enriched in the translation. The counts follow the print: twelve nights, then sixteen (84) and a month (85) as the views of others.

hindi: अन्य लोगों के अनुसार सोलह रात।
english: According to others, sixteen nights.
notes: Elliptical; 'iti anye' marks the opinion of others, so 'according to others' is a plain rendering; no verb in the Sanskrit. Refers to the length of the ṛtu of unit 83. The number is as printed.

hindi: जिसके योनि, गर्भाशय और आर्तव शुद्ध हों, उसके लिए कुछ लोगों के अनुसार एक मास भी।
english: But, according to some, even a month, of (the one) whose yoni, womb (garbhāśaya) and ārtava are pure.

text_flags.why: possible: the visarga is missing; the genitive singular is ārtavāyāḥ

notes: GROUPING: the unit appears to continue units 83-84 (the length of the ṛtu). The feminine bahuvrīhi implies a woman; it is shown as 'the one'. garbhāśaya = womb (standard), literally 'seat of the embryo'. 'Some' states an opinion; no verb in the Sanskrit.

hindi: अन्य लोगों के अनुसार उसी प्रकार अदृष्ट आर्तव वाला भी होता है।
english: According to others, in the same way there is also one with ārtava not seen.
notes: 'iti apare' marks the opinion of others. The unstated noun is shown as 'one' (it agrees with ṛtu, masculine). 'tadvat' is read as 'in the same way'; what it is likened to (the length of the ṛtu of 83-84 or the month of 85) is not stated. The printed unit begins 'tadvada…' with the sandhi tadvat + adṛṣṭa.

hindi: कृश और प्रसन्न मुख वाली, फड़कते हुए श्रोणि यानी कूल्हों और स्तनों वाली जिस स्त्री की आँखें और कुक्षि शिथिल हों और जिसे पुरुष की कामना हो, उसे ऋतुमती स्त्री जानना चाहिए।
english: (A woman) with a lean, clear face, and with throbbing hips and breasts, One should know that woman to be in her ṛtu (season), a ṛtumatī who has drooping eyes and belly and desire for a man.

text_flags.why: possible: 'akṣu' is not a word; 'akṣi' (eye) is the expected member
possible: accusative feminine expected to agree with 'striyam'; final anusvāra apparently dropped

notes: [02.01.87] Accusative feminine bahuvrīhi, the object of 'vidyāt' in unit 88. GROUPING: this unit appears to continue in 88. 'payodhara' (lit. 'water-bearer') = breast (standard). 'śroṇi' = hip/pelvic region (standard). Printed fused 'sphuracchroṇi' read as sphurat+śroṇi (ch- from sandhi). [02.01.88] GROUPING: continues 87 (the accusative descriptions in 87 and here qualify 'striyam'). 'kukṣi' = belly/flank. 'ṛtumatī' = a woman in her ṛtu (season); in ch01 u83 the ṛtu is the twelve nights counted from the ārtava being seen (standard sense).

hindi: जैसे दिन बीत जाने पर कमल संकोच को प्राप्त होता है, वैसे ही ऋतुकाल बीत जाने पर वह योनि भीतर शुक्र को ग्रहण नहीं करती।
english: As a lotus comes to contraction when the day has passed, so when the ṛtu (season) has passed, that yoni (vagina) does not receive semen (śukra) inside.

text_flags.why: possible: 'kṛtāvatīte' is not a sensible compound; ṛtau atīte (when the ṛtu is past) fits the sense and the comparison with the lotus after the day has passed; initial k- probably an added or misread letter

notes: [02.01.89] GROUPING: the comparison is completed in 90 ('yoniḥ sā ...'). 'dine atīte' locative absolute. [02.01.90] Completes the comparison of 89. 'yoni' = womb / female genital passage (probable; the exact organ is not specified by the word). The restored 'ṛtau atīte' rests on one conjectured letter.

from the mouth of the yoni

hindi: एक मास में संचित रक्त को, ऋतुकाल में फिर, दो धमनियों द्वारा थोड़े काले और दुर्गन्ध वाले को वायु योनि के मुख से निकालता है।
english: Blood accumulated over a month, again in the ṛtu (season), by the two dhamanīs (vessels), slightly dark and ill-smelling, wind (vāyu) would discharge from the mouth of the yoni.

text_flags.why: possible: 'sṛdet' is not a verb form; opt. 3 sg. of √sṛj 'send out' fits the sense (d for j is a common OCR/print confusion)

notes: [02.01.91] GROUPING: the sentence is completed in 92 (verb 'sṛdet'). 'upacitaṃ raktaṃ' agree. dhamanī = a vessel or channel (probable; whether artery, vein or other duct is not stated); the text says only 'the two' and names neither. The exact case sense of 'dhamanībhyām' (instrumental dual) is by means of the two vessels. [02.01.92] Completes 91: the object is the blood (raktam) of 91. This unit is the verb phrase of that sentence. Hindi uses the plain present for the optative.

words.gloss: at the sight of the flower (puṣpa), i.e. menstruation
sleeping on a spread of darbha grass

hindi: तब पुष्पदर्शन यानी रजोदर्शन होने पर पहले दिन से ही ब्रह्मचारिणी रहे, स्नान और अलंकार से रहित, दर्भ यानी सम्भवतः कुश के बिछौने पर सोती हुई, तीन रात तक रहे।
english: Then, when the flower is seen (puṣpadarśana: the onset of menstruation), from the first day onward she should remain a chaste woman (brahmacāriṇī), without bathing and ornaments, sleeping on a spread of darbha grass, for three nights.
notes: Prose unit; the subject (the woman, 'strī') is not named and is understood from the context. 'puṣpa' (flower) is the usual word for the menstrual flow; 'puṣpadarśana' = first sight of menses (standard). 'āsīta' is 'should stay / sit', here 'remain'. darbha = a sacred grass, usually kuśa (Desmostachya bipinnata); some sources give Imperata cylindrica for darbha (identity disputed).
lines_deva: ततः पुष्पदर्शने प्रथमदिवसात्प्रभृति ब्रह्मचारिणी स्नानालंकाररहिता दर्भसंस्तरशायिनी त्रिरात्रमासीत

hindi: और पत्ते के दोने या हथेली, इनमें से किसी एक में, दूध के साथ पकाया हुआ थोड़ा यावक यानी सम्भवतः यव से बना एक पदार्थ, कृश करने के लिए खाए।
english: And, in one of the two, a leaf-bowl or the palm of the hand, she should eat a little yāvaka (probably a barley preparation) cooked with milk, for the purpose of thinning (karśana).

text_flags.why: possible: two words printed joined without a space; no letter changed

notes: 'yāvaka' is probably a preparation of yava, barley (probable); the word can also mean lac, but that does not suit eating. 'anyatame' with the two nouns is taken as 'in either one of the two'. Subject (the woman of 93) is understood. 'karśana' = making lean/thin.

hindi: तीखे, गरम, खट्टे और नमकीन को त्याग दे।
english: She should avoid sharp, hot, sour and salty (ones).
notes: Subject (the woman of 93) and the nouns (food) are understood. The compound is a dvandva of four qualities; 'tīkṣṇa' = sharp/pungent.

english: On the fourth day, rubbed with unguent powder, bathed in cold water, anointed, adorned, wearing white garlands and garments, with auspicious rites and benedictions performed, with her mind on no other, she should look upon a husband of just this kind.

words.gloss: desiring a son with good qualities

hindi: क्योंकि उस समय वह जिस प्रकार के को ही देखती या सोचती है, वैसे को ही जन्म देती है। अनुमानित पाठ पर, तब स्नान के बाद, फिर से, गुणवान् पुत्र की इच्छा वाला चार रात बीतने दे।
english: For then, whatever kind (of one) she sees or thinks of, a (one) of that kind she bears. Then, after the bath, again, one desiring a son with good qualities should let four nights pass (on a conjectural reading).

text_flags.why: possible: an anusvāra before t- is the print's usual way of writing n; here the ablative -āt is meant
possible: long ū is not expected in catur-rātra (four nights)

notes: [02.01.97] Objects are unstated ('yādṛśam', 'tādṛśam' are adjectives); the sense is the kind of person seen or thought of, and a like child. Closing 'iti' marks the end of the statement; not translated. [02.01.98] 'upekṣeta' (look over, disregard, let pass) is read as letting four nights go by; this is a conjectural sense in context (counting with 99-100 reaches the 8th night). The subject is not stated: 'putrārthī' is masculine, but the form is the general one. 'snātāt' (ablative of snāta, 'after the bath') is an unusual form. GROUPING: this unit appears to continue with 99 and 100. Reviewer: upekṣeta (upa-√īkṣ) usually means 'disregard, abstain from, neglect'. A possible alternative reading is snātāṃ (f. acc., 'the bathed woman') with the t as a stray letter, giving 'should abstain from the bathed woman for four nights'; undecided, for the owner.

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर: पुष्प के दिन से सात रात।
english: From the day of the flower (menstruation), seven nights (on a conjectural reading).

notes: Fragment without a verb; GROUPING: appears to belong with 98 (the nights to let pass) and to lead on to 100. No verb is supplied.

hindi: फिर आठवीं, दसवीं अथवा बारहवीं रात में पुत्र की कामना वाला सहवास करे।
english: Then, on the eighth, tenth or twelfth night, one desiring a son should lie together.
notes: 'rātrau' is singular and understood with each ordinal. The object of 'saṃviśet' is not stated.
lines_deva: अथाष्टम्यां दशम्यां द्वादश्यां वा रात्रौ पुत्रकामः संविशेत्
lines_iast: athāṣṭamyāṃ daśamyāṃ dvādaśyāṃ vā rātrau putrakāmaḥ saṃviśet

hindi: पाँचवीं, सातवीं या नवीं रात में पुत्री की कामना वाला।
english: On the fifth, seventh or ninth (night), one desiring a daughter.
notes: Elliptic: the verb 'saṃviśet' and the word 'rātrau' are carried from unit 100; no verb is supplied in the translation. GROUPING: this unit appears to continue 100.

words.gloss: in progressive order, each later one more

hindi: उन रातों में उत्तरोत्तर सन्तान को आयु, आरोग्य, ऐश्वर्य, सौभाग्य, बल, वर्ण यानी रंग और इन्द्रियों की सम्पदा प्राप्त होती है।
english: In these (nights), progressively, the offspring has the endowment of life-span, health, lordship, good fortune, strength, complexion (varṇa) and the sense faculties.
notes: 'apatyasya bhavati' is a genitive of possession ('there is to the offspring'). 'saṃpad' is read as the last member of one long dvandva-plus compound, 'endowment of' the whole list. 'varṇa' = complexion (probable; it can also mean colour or class).

hindi: किन्तु इसके आगे तो आयु आदि का उत्तरोत्तर ही ह्रास होता है।
english: But after this there is a progressive decrease of life-span and the rest.
notes: Copula understood. 'ādi' = 'and the rest', that is the list in 102. GROUPING: follows 102.

words.gloss: ārtava (menstrual blood, the female generative fluid; standard)

hindi: उनमें सम रात्रियों में आर्तव यानी मासिक रक्तस्राव अल्प हो जाता है और विषम रात्रियों में बढ़ता है।
english: Among these, in the even nights the ārtava (menstrual blood) becomes small; in the odd (ones) it increases.
notes: 'rātriṣu' is understood with 'ayugmāsu'. ārtava = menstrual blood / female generative fluid (standard). The subject of 'āpyāyate' is the same ārtava.

hindi: इसलिए उन रात्रियों में क्रम से पुत्र का और पुत्री का जन्म होता है।
english: Therefore in these (nights), in order, there is the birth of a son and of a daughter.
notes: Copula understood. 'kramāt' = in the order (even/odd) of the nights; the pairing 'son : even / daughter : odd' is not spelled out in this unit. 'tāsu' refers back to the nights of 100-104.

words.gloss: one in whom the sight of ārtava has not ceased

hindi: और इसीलिए जिस स्त्री का आर्तव दिखना बन्द नहीं हुआ है, उसके पास पुत्र की इच्छा वाला विषम दिनों में भी न जाए।
english: And for this very reason one desiring a son should not approach a woman in whom the sight of the ārtava (menstrual blood) has not ceased, even on odd days.
notes: The woman is the bahuvrīhi in the accusative, 'one whose seeing of ārtava has not stopped'. 'ahassu' is a printed variant of ahaḥsu. The unit speaks of days, the earlier ones of nights; the text is followed as printed.

hindi: किन्तु यदि आहार के अनुसार विषम रात्रियों में शुक्र की अधिकता और सम रात्रियों में कमी हो, तब पुरुष स्त्री के आकार वाला, दुर्बल या हीन अंगों वाला उत्पन्न होता है।
english: But if, owing to conformity to diet, there is an abundance of semen (śukra) in the odd (nights) and a deficiency in the even ones, then a male is born of female form, weak, or deficient in limb.

text_flags.why: possible: two words printed fused; no letter changed

notes: 'āhāra-anurodha' is read as 'conformity to / following the diet'; the sense of the cause is not fully clear. 'rātriṣu' understood with ayugmāsu, yugmāsu. 'tataḥpumān' is printed fused (tataḥ pumān).
lines_deva: यदि त्वाहारानुरोधादयुग्मासु शुक्रस्याधिक्यता युग्मासु च न्यूनता स्यात् ततःपुमान् स्त्र्याकृतिर्दुर्बलो हीनांगो वा जायते
lines_iast: yadi tvāhārānurodhādayugmāsu śukrasyādhikyatā yugmāsu ca nyūnatā syāt tataḥpumān stryākṛtirdurbalo hīnāṃgo vā jāyate

words.gloss: napuṃsaka (a person who is neither male nor female; eunuch, impotent; standard)

hindi: और स्त्री पुरुष के आकार वाली, दुर्बल या हीन अंगों वाली। किन्तु ग्यारहवीं और तेरहवीं रात में नपुंसक होगा।
english: And a female of male form, weak, or deficient in limb. But on the eleventh and thirteenth (nights) there would be a napuṃsaka (a person neither male nor female; eunuch).
notes: [02.01.108] Elliptic: the verb 'jāyate' is carried from 107 and not supplied. GROUPING: continues 107. 'durbalāhīnāṃgī' is printed fused (durbalā hīnāṅgī); no letter wrong. [02.01.109] 'rātriṣu' understood. 'napuṃsaka' (lit. 'non-male') also is the grammatical term for neuter; here a person is meant. The Hindi word नपुंसक covers impotent and eunuch, as does the Sanskrit.

words.gloss: relating to a son, for obtaining a son

hindi: तब उपाध्याय यानी शिक्षक पुत्र सम्बन्धी विधान का आचरण करे।
english: Then the teacher (upādhyāya) should perform the procedure relating to a son (putrīya).
notes: 'putrīya' is the adjective 'relating to a son'. The rite itself is not described in this unit; the 'upādhyāya' is a teacher/preceptor (probable; he may act as the officiating priest).

hindi: किन्तु शुद्ध हुई स्त्री के लिए मन्त्र से रहित।
english: But for the purified woman, devoid of mantra.

text_flags.why: possible: a neuter -m ending may have been lost; read as 'mantra-varjitam', but the printed form is also usable as a stem

notes: Fragment with no verb and no stated noun; the sense is probably that the procedure for the purified woman is without a mantra (conjectural). 'śuddhā' = purified (apparently after the bath of 96). GROUPING: appears to belong with 110 (the procedure), unclear how. Reviewer conjecture (undecided): śuddhāyāstu may be an OCR misreading of śūdrāyās tu ('but for a śūdra woman, without mantra'); dr/ddh confusion is recorded in the glossary.

words.gloss: having the form, complexion and conduct of that (son)

hindi: और जिस प्रकार के पुत्र की वह आशा करे, उसके रूप, वर्ण और आचरण वाले जनपदों का चिन्तन करो, इस प्रकार स्त्री से कहना चाहिए।
english: And the woman is to be told: 'Think upon the janapadas (regions or their peoples) that have the form, complexion and conduct of whatever kind of son you may wish for.'
notes: 'janapada' = a region or its people (standard); both senses are possible. The 'iti' closes the quoted instruction. The 'tad' in the compound refers to the wished-for son.
lines_deva: यादृशं च पुत्रमाशासीत तद्रूपवर्णचरितान् जनपदानुचिंतयेति स्त्री वाच्या
lines_iast: yādṛśaṃ ca putramāśāsīta tadrūpavarṇacaritān janapadānuciṃtayeti strī vācyā

hindi: और उस जनपद के आहार, विहार, उपचार और परिच्छद का अनुसरण करे।
english: And she should follow the food, way of living (vihāra), practices (upacāra) and accessories (paricchada) of that region.
notes: The printed whole is one fused token; it is read as dvandva 'āhāra-vihāra-upacāra-paricchada' attached to 'tad-janapada', then 'ca' and the verb. The English glosses for vihāra, upacāra and paricchada are the plainest senses; each has others (e.g. upacāra = treatment / service; paricchada = retinue, apparel). Subject (the woman) understood from 112.

words.gloss: at the end of the rite (karman)
in a part of the night

hindi: और कर्म के अन्त में पुरुष एक मास ब्रह्मचारी रहकर, घी और दूध के साथ शालि का भात खाकर, अधिक न खाया हुआ, सुखी, माला पहने, प्रसन्न मन वाला, तृप्त अंगों वाला, श्वेत वस्त्र पहने, मुहूर्त जानने वाले को मान्य रात्रि के भाग में, कल्याणकारी बातें सोचता हुआ, उसकी कामना वाला, भली-भाँति बिछी शय्या पर दाहिने पैर से पूर्व की ओर चढ़े।
english: And at the end of the rite, the man, chaste for a month, having eaten boiled śāli rice with ghee and milk, not over-fed, happy, wearing a garland, cheerful, with limbs refreshed, in white clothes, in a part of the night approved by the muhūrta-expert (astrologer), thinking of auspicious things, desirous of that, should mount the well-spread bed with the right foot, toward the east.

text_flags.why: possible: 'karmāte' is not a word; anusvāra/n lost before t (karma-anta)
possible: 'abhiprāiya' is not a form; the gerund of abhi-pra-√aś 'having eaten' fits (ś misread as i)
possible: only the anusvāra spelling of ṅ; no change in sense

notes: Long single prose sentence with one main verb 'ārohet' (should mount). 'prāk' can mean 'toward the east' or 'first, forward'; the parallel 115 uses 'pūrvam' for 'first', so 'east' is taken. 'karmānta' (end of the rite) is taken from the corrected reading and its object rite is not named here. 'mauhūrtika' = one skilled in muhūrta (timing); astrologer (standard). 'śāli' = a kind of rice (Oryza sativa, standard) and 'odana' = boiled rice. 'tad-abhikāma' = desiring 'that' (the union), literal. 'ca' in 'karmāte ca' is read as 'and'. Subject: the man.
lines_deva: कर्माते च पुमान्मासंब्रह्मचारी सर्पिःक्षीराभ्यां शाल्योदनमभिप्राइय नात्याशितः सुखीस्रग्वी सुमनाः प्रीणितांगः शुक्लनिवसनो मौहूर्तिकानुमते रात्रिभागे कल्याणानि चिंतयंस्तदभिकामः स्वास्तीर्णं शयनं दक्षिणेन पादेन प्रागारोहेत्
lines_iast: karmāte ca pumānmāsaṃbrahmacārī sarpiḥkṣīrābhyāṃ śālyodanamabhiprāiya nātyāśitaḥ sukhīsragvī sumanāḥ prīṇitāṃgaḥ śuklanivasano mauhūrtikānumate rātribhāge kalyāṇāni ciṃtayaṃstadabhikāmaḥ svāstīrṇaṃ śayanaṃ dakṣiṇena pādena prāgārohet

words.gloss: with oil and māṣa (black gram) as the chief food

hindi: उसी प्रकार की स्त्री, कृश अंगों वाली, तेल और माष यानी उड़द प्रधान आहार वाली, पहले बाएँ पैर से पुरुष के दाहिनी ओर शय्या पर चढ़े।
english: And the woman, of that very kind, with limbs made thin and with oil and māṣa (black gram) as the chief food, should first ascend the bed with the left foot, on the right of the man.

text_flags.why: possible: two words printed fused; no letter changed

notes: 'tad-vidhā eva' = of just that kind, i.e. prepared in the same way as the man. 'uttara' in 'uttarāhāra' = chief or additional/following: here 'chief' is taken (conjectural). māṣa = black gram, Vigna mungo (standard). 'dakṣiṇataḥ' is taken with 'puruṣasya' as 'on the man's right'.
lines_deva: तद्विधैव च प्रमदा कर्शितांगी तैलमाषोत्तराहारा पूर्वं वामपादेनपुरुषस्य दक्षिणतः शय्यामधिरोहेत्
lines_iast: tadvidhaiva ca pramadā karśitāṃgī tailamāṣottarāhārā pūrvaṃ vāmapādenapuruṣasya dakṣiṇataḥ śayyāmadhirohet

hindi: वहाँ मन्त्र का प्रयोग करे।
english: There one should employ the mantra.
notes: The subject is not stated; the man is probably meant (conjectural). The mantra is given in 117.

words.gloss: ahi (serpent; sense in the mantra unclear)

hindi: तुम अहि हो, तुम आयु हो, तुम सब ओर प्रतिष्ठा यानी आधार हो। धाता तुम्हें स्थापित करे, विधाता तुम्हें स्थापित करे। ब्रह्मवर्चस से युक्त होओ।
english: You are the ahi; you are life; you are the support on every side. May Dhātṛ place you; may Vidhātṛ place you. Be with brahma-splendour (brahmavarcas).

text_flags.why: possible: the mantra is elsewhere read 'ahir asi'; the long ā looks like a print or transcription slip

notes: This is the mantra announced in 116. The sense of 'ahi' here is unclear (serpent is the plain meaning; the word is kept). 'dadhātu' has no stated object in the Sanskrit beyond 'tvā'. 'brahmavarcasā bhava' = 'be with brahmavarcas'. Closing 'iti' ends the mantra and is not translated.
lines_deva: आहिरसि आयुरसि सर्वतः प्रतिष्ठासि धाता त्वा दधातु विधाता त्वा दधातुब्रह्मवर्चसा भवेति
lines_iast: āhirasi āyurasi sarvataḥ pratiṣṭhāsi dhātā tvā dadhātu vidhātā tvā dadhātubrahmavarcasā bhaveti

hindi: ब्रह्मा, बृहस्पति, विष्णु, सोम, सूर्य तथा दोनों अश्विनीकुमार, भग, फिर मित्र और वरुण, मुझे वीर पुत्र प्रदान करें।
english: Brahmā, Bṛhaspati, Viṣṇu, Soma, Sūrya, and also the two Aśvins, Bhaga, and then Mitra and Varuṇa: may they bestow on me a heroic son.
notes: [02.01.118] A list of deities, the subject of 'dadhatu' in 119. GROUPING: appears to continue 117 (the mantra) and to be completed by 119. [02.01.119] Completes the list begun in 118; the subject of 'dadhatu' is the deities named in 118-119 (appears to continue 118). 'me' is taken as 'for me'. Closing 'iti' ends the mantra and is not translated.
lines_deva: भगोऽथ मित्रावरुणौ वीरं दधतु मे सुतमिति
lines_iast: bhago'tha mitrāvaruṇau vīraṃ dadhatu me sutamiti

hindi: तब परस्पर मधुर वचनों से सान्त्वना देकर, हर्ष के साथ, अनुकूल रीति से दोनों सहवास करें।
english: Then, having soothed each other with gentle words, they two should lie together, with joy and agreeably.

text_flags.why: possible: 'saṃvesetām' is not a regular form; the dual optative of sam-√viś (cf. 'saṃviśet' in 100) is meant

notes: 'sāman' here means conciliatory or gentle speech (probable; it can also be a Vedic chant). The dual shows both partners are the subject.

hindi: और अन्त में इसे अचानक ठण्डे जल से सींचे।
english: And at the end he should suddenly sprinkle her with cold water.

text_flags.why: possible: 'paryānta' with long ā is not the usual form (paryanta)
possible: long ā in the prefix pari- is not expected

notes: The subject is not stated; the man is understood (conjectural). 'enām' refers to the woman.

hindi: इस विषय में, अधिक खाई हुई, भूखी, प्यासी, डरी हुई, उदास मन वाली, शोक से पीड़ित, क्रोधित, अत्यन्त स्थूल, किसी दूसरे की कामना वाली अथवा सहवास की इच्छा न रखने वाली स्त्री गर्भ धारण नहीं करती, या दोषयुक्त गर्भ धारण करती है।
english: In this matter, a woman who is over-fed, hungry, thirsty, frightened, dejected, afflicted by grief, angry, very fat, desiring another, or desiring no intercourse, does not bear a foetus (garbha), or bears a defective one.

text_flags.why: possible: final anusvāra lost; accusative singular expected as object of 'dhatte'

notes: 'atimedurā' is read as 'very fat / very unctuous' (probable; medura = smooth, fatty). 'avyavāya' = absence of intercourse (vyavāya = sexual union, standard). 'viguṇa' = faulty, defective. The two 'vā' join the list members and the two outcomes.
lines_deva: तत्रात्याशिता क्षुधिता पिपासिता भीता विमनाः शोकार्ता क्रुद्धाऽतिमेदुरा ऽन्यकामाऽव्यवायकामा वान गर्भ धत्ते विगुणं वा
lines_iast: tatrātyāśitā kṣudhitā pipāsitā bhītā vimanāḥ śokārtā kruddhā'timedurā 'nyakāmā'vyavāyakāmā vāna garbha dhatte viguṇaṃ vā

hindi: इसी प्रकार पुरुष भी; और वह नीचे न रहे। क्योंकि इस प्रकार स्त्री की चेष्टा वाला पुरुष उत्पन्न होता है, अथवा पुरुष की चेष्टा वाली स्त्री।
english: Likewise the man also; and he should not stay below. For thus a male is born with a woman's behaviour, or a female with a man's behaviour.
notes: [02.01.123] The first clause has no verb. The sense is probably that the man too should not be in the states listed in 122 (conjectural); no verb is supplied. 'adhaḥ' = below, that is, under the woman (probable). [02.01.124] Gives the stated result of the man staying below in 123 (the link 'tathā hi' = 'for thus'). GROUPING: follows 123.
lines_deva: तथा हि स्त्रीचेष्टः पुमान् जायते पुंचेष्टा वा स्त्री
lines_iast: tathā hi strīceṣṭaḥ pumān jāyate puṃceṣṭā vā strī

hindi: और औंधी पड़ी हुई अथवा करवट पर पड़ी हुई स्त्री का सेवन न करे।
english: And one should not resort to a woman lying face down or lying on her side.
notes: 'nyubja' = face down, prone. 'seveta' = resort to, have union with; the object (the woman) is the accusative feminine. The subject is not stated (the man is probably meant).
lines_deva: न च न्युब्जां पार्श्वगतां वा सेवेत
lines_iast: na ca nyubjāṃ pārśvagatāṃ vā seveta

hindi: औंधी पड़ी हुई स्त्री में वात बलवान है; वह योनि को पीड़ित करता है।
english: In one lying face down Vāta is strong; it presses (afflicts) the yoni (vagina).
notes: Vāta is one of the three doṣas (kept, no modern equivalent). 'yoni' is the female genital passage/womb (probable). Copula understood in the first clause.
lines_deva: न्युब्जायां वातो बलवान् स योनिं पीडयति
lines_iast: nyubjāyāṃ vāto balavān sa yoniṃ pīḍayati

words.gloss: of one lying on the right side

hindi: दाहिनी करवट पर पड़ी हुई स्त्री का श्लेष्मा यानी कफ दबकर च्युत होकर गर्भाशय को बन्द कर देता है।
english: In one lying on the right side, Kapha (śleṣman), pressed and displaced, closes the womb (garbhāśaya).
notes: 'śleṣman' = Kapha (standard synonym). 'garbhāśaya' = womb/uterus (standard). 'cyuta' = fallen away from its place. 'apidadhāti' can be 'covers' or 'closes up'; the plainer 'closes' is used.

words.gloss: of one lying on the left side

hindi: बायीं करवट पर पड़ी हुई स्त्री का पित्त उसी प्रकार रक्त और शुक्र को जलाता है।
english: In one lying on the left side, similarly Pitta scorches the blood (rakta) and the semen (śukra).

text_flags.why: possible: 'śuke' is not a word; the neuter dual 'rakta-śukre' (blood and semen) fits sense and metre

notes: 'vi-dah' = burns up, scorches (rakta-śukre as dual objects). 'tadvat' = similarly to 126-127. Pitta is a doṣa (kept).

hindi: इसलिए चित लेटी हुई स्त्री बीज यानी सम्भवतः शुक्र को ग्रहण करे।
english: Therefore, lying on her back, she should receive the seed (bīja; probably semen).

text_flags.why: likely: 'dasmāt' is not a word; t misprinted d (ta/da confusion)
