words.gloss: by conformity to country and family

hindi: और देश तथा कुल के अनुवर्तन से रंग का भेद।
english: And, by conformity to country and family, difference of colour.
notes: Elliptical (no verb). varṇa = colour (of the skin); not 'caste' here, since the preceding units speak of fair, dark and dusky.

words.gloss: from contact with the water and space elements
from contact with earth and air
in the balance of all the elements

hindi: वैसे ही तेजस् धातु के जल और आकाश धातु से संपर्क से गौरता; पृथ्वी और वायु के संपर्क से कालापन; सब धातुओं की समता में साँवलापन।
english: Likewise, from the contact of the fire element (tejas-dhātu) with the water and space elements, fairness; from contact with earth and air, darkness; when all the elements are in balance, dusky colour.
notes: dhātu here = element (the great elements: fire, water, space, earth, air), not the bodily tissue dhātu. 'of it' in the second clause (the fire element) is understood from the first clause and not stated; the text says only 'from contact with earth and air'. Elliptical (no verb).
lines_deva: तथा तेजोधातोरुदकाकाशधातुसंपर्काद्गौरता भूवायुसंपर्कात् कृष्णता सर्वधातुसाम्ये श्यामता
lines_iast: tathā tejodhātorudakākāśadhātusaṃparkādgauratā bhūvāyusaṃparkāt kṛṣṇatā sarvadhātusāmye śyāmatā

words.gloss: bringing about special features of sattva (mind)
the sattva of mother and father

hindi: सत्त्व यानी मन में विशेषता लाने वाले, फिर माता और पिता का सत्त्व, गर्भवती के बार-बार श्रवण, अपना संचित कर्म होता है, और पूर्व अभ्यास।
english: Again, (ones) bringing about special features of sattva (mind): the sattva of the mother and father, the repeated hearings of the pregnant woman; one's own accumulated action (karma) is, and past practice.

text_flags.why: satva is a spelling of sattva (normalised in words, also in mātāpitṛsatvāni); viśeṣa is correct as printed
possible: 'antairvatnyāḥ' for antarvatnyāḥ (pregnant woman); ar lost as ai
possible: final m lost; the comma is a print mark

notes: The sentence is a list of causes of the nature of the child's sattva; 'bhavati' (is) stands after karma and is translated literally; the sentence is not smoothed. sattva = mind, mental constitution (standard). śruti here = what is heard (hearing); it is not stated what is heard.
lines_deva: सत्वविशेषकराणि पुनर्मातापितृसत्वान्यंतैर्वत्न्याः श्रुतयश्चाभीक्ष्ण, स्वोपचितं कर्म भवति पूर्वाभ्यासश्चेति
lines_iast: satvaviśeṣakarāṇi punarmātāpitṛsatvānyaṃtairvatnyāḥ śrutayaścābhīkṣṇa, svopacitaṃ karma bhavati pūrvābhyāsaśceti

hindi: और इस विषय में होते हैं।
english: And in this matter there are (verses).
notes: Formula introducing the verses that follow; the noun 'verses' is not in the Sanskrit and is shown only in brackets.

words.gloss: ārtava (menstrual blood, the female reproductive element; probable)

hindi: घी, दूध आदि, मत्त्यासु नामक अस्पष्ट शब्द, प्रसन्न, कफ स्वभाव वालों में आर्तव यानी स्त्री का रज देर तक ठहरता है; विपरीतों में इससे अन्यथा।
english: Ghee, milk and the like, mattyāsu (unclear word), in cheerful (ones), in (ones) whose nature is Kapha The ārtava (menstrual blood, the female element) stays long; in the opposite (ones), otherwise than this.

text_flags.why: possible: ā shortened before di; ghṛta-kṣīra-ādi
possible: damaged word; a form ending in -āsu (feminine locative plural) agreeing with muditāsu; not restored

notes: [02.01.157] GROUPING: the sentence appears to continue in 158 ('the ārtava stays long'). The words ghṛta-kṣīra-ādi and mattyāsu are not joined into a firm sense: mattyāsu is damaged and is not interpreted. The feminine plural endings (muditāsu) show that women are meant, but the noun is not stated. The sentence appears to be completed in 158. [02.01.158] GROUPING: appears to complete 157. What the ārtava stays in is not stated. ārtava = menstrual blood / female reproductive fluid (probable; the text itself gives no more).

hindi: गिरने मात्र से ही रंग ग्रहण करता है, जैसे स्वच्छ वस्त्र। निश्चित रूप से, अनुमानित पाठ पर गर्भ, वैसे ही बीज, क्षेत्र, तैयार किया हुआ बीज।
english: From the mere falling (nipāta) it takes up colour, as a clean cloth does. Certainly, on a conjectural reading the foetus, likewise the seed, the field, the prepared seed.

text_flags.why: possible: the s of garbhas lost before tathā; garbhaḥ tathā

notes: [02.01.159] The subject of gṛhṇāti is not stated (presumably the ārtava of 158 or the receiving element); not decided. 'nipāta' = falling (of the dye / of the fluid); not explained in the text. [02.01.160] No verb; the line is elliptical and the connection between the terms is not stated. The field-and-seed pairing is the imagery of the tradition but the text here only lists the terms; no sense is built on it. dhruvam may be adverb 'certainly' or adjective 'sure' (agreeing with garbhaḥ). Review: upaskṛtam (n. sg.) could also agree with kṣetram and bījam together ('field and seed, prepared'); the translation keeps the plain list.

hindi: दैव के अविरुद्ध रहने पर, निश्चित रूप से, काल में, प्रयुक्त कर्म की सिद्धि; इस कारण पुंसवन आदि को प्रकट होने से पहले प्रयोग में लाए।
english: When fate (daiva) is unopposed, certainly, in time, of an applied action Success; therefore one should apply puṃsavana and the like before manifestation.

text_flags.why: possible: final m lost

notes: [02.01.161] GROUPING: the sentence appears to continue in 162 ('siddhiḥ', success), so the subject 'success' is in the next unit. daiva = fate (what is due to previous action); not explained here. [02.01.162] GROUPING: appears to complete 161 (siddhiḥ). 'vyakteḥ' is the manifestation (of the foetus) as in 131; the foetus is not named in this unit. puṃsavana = rite for obtaining a male child (see 131). Review: puṃsavanādyasmāt is read puṃsavana-ādi + asmāt ('therefore'), not yasmāt.
lines_deva: अविरुद्धे ध्रुवं दैवे काले युक्तस्य कर्मणः
lines_iast: aviruddhe dhruvaṃ daive kāle yuktasya karmaṇaḥ

hindi: और इस प्रकार जन्मे हुए रूपवान, महान् सत्त्व वाले और दीर्घायु होते हैं। अच्छे पुत्र ऋण से मुक्त कराने वाले हों, पुत्र वालों द्वारा माने गए।
english: And those born thus are beautiful, of great sattva (mind), long-lived. Good sons would be releasers from debt, regarded by those who have sons.
notes: [02.01.163] No verb is stated (elliptical); the plural 'born (ones)' is read as people, since the following adjectives are masculine plural. rūpa = form/beauty. [02.01.164] 'putriṇām matāḥ' is read as 'regarded (so) by those who have sons' (genitive of the agent with a past participle); the alternative 'accounted among those with sons' is possible. ṛṇa = debt; the kind of debt is not stated. Review: suputrāḥ is taken as the subject of syuḥ and matāḥ; the alternative division 'they would be releasers from debt; good sons are so regarded by those who have sons' needs a supplied subject and 'so'.

words.gloss: devoted to the gods, conduct, purity and the like
through connection with practice of a former birth

hindi: जो देवताओं, आचार, शौच आदि में रत है, वह महान् गुणों वाले को जन्म देती है। इसी प्रकार आचरण किया हुआ पूर्व जन्म के अभ्यास के योग से दौड़ता है।
english: She who is devoted to the gods, conduct, purity and the like bears (one) of great qualities. In this way, and what is practised runs (dhāvati) through its connection with practice from a former birth.
notes: [02.01.165] The noun 'woman' is understood from the feminine ratā and is not stated; 'one of great qualities' (child) is shown without a noun for the same reason. The compound is read 'devoted to (the worship of) gods, conduct, purity, etc.'; daivata may be taken with ācāra as 'conduct towards the gods'. [02.01.166] Word order is as printed: 'dhāvati evaṃ ca ācaritam'. dhāvati (runs, moves; also 'washes') is read as 'runs on / is carried on'; the sentence is hard and the sense is not made firm. prāgjanma = former birth (alternatively 'birth before'); not decided.

words.gloss: śukra (semen; here of women, so reproductive fluid)

hindi: स्त्रियाँ भी पुरुष के साथ समागम में शुक्र यानी प्रजनन द्रव का स्राव करती ही हैं। वह गर्भ के लिए कुछ भी नहीं करता, ऐसा नहीं सोचा जाता।
english: Women too indeed discharge śukra (semen; here of women, the reproductive fluid) at union with a man. It is not thought that it does nothing at all for the foetus.
notes: [02.01.167] śukra is normally semen (standard); applied to women it is read as the reproductive fluid. 'puṃsaḥ samāgame' = 'at union with a man' (genitive with samāgama). [02.01.168] 'That' is the śukra of 167. The double negation is as printed: 'tat garbhasya na kiñcit karoti' = it does nothing for the foetus; 'iti na cintyate' = this is not thought.
lines_deva: गर्भस्य तन्न किंचित्तु करोतीति न चिंत्यते
lines_iast: garbhasya tanna kiṃcittu karotīti na ciṃtyate

words.gloss: named Putrakāmīya (relating to the desire for a son)

hindi: इस प्रकार पुत्रकामीय नामक प्रथम अध्याय।
english: Thus the first chapter, named Putrakāmīya.
notes: Colophon. 'Putrakāmīya' = 'relating to the desire for a son'. The closing iti is a colophon marker.
